title: Former Coinbase Investment Chief Now Manages Evernorth’s 473M XRP
summary: A former Coinbase Asset Management co-chief investment officer now directs Evernorth’s treasury, which held approximately 473 million XRP at closing. His appointment brings institutional trading experience to a Nasdaq-listed company pursuing active cryptocurrency investment strategies. Former Coinba...
content:
A former Coinbase Asset Management co-chief investment officer now directs Evernorth’s treasury, which held approximately 473 million XRP at closing. His appointment brings institutional trading experience to a Nasdaq-listed company pursuing active cryptocurrency investment strategies.

Key Takeaways

  • Hugo Jeandesboz leads a treasury that held about 473 million XRP at closing.
  • His responsibilities span allocation, liquidity, trading and custody relationships.
  • Evernorth targets growth in XRP per share through active investment strategies.

Former Coinbase Executive Takes Charge of Evernorth’s XRP

An XRP treasury holding approximately 473 million tokens at closing now has a former Coinbase Asset Management executive directing its investment strategy. Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) announced on Oct. 12 that it appointed Hugo Jeandesboz as chief investment officer. He reports to founder and CEO Asheesh Birla and oversees allocation, liquidity management, and active management of the company’s holdings.

Birla said:

“Hugo brings distinct experience that aligns with our active treasury strategy.”

The position also makes Jeandesboz the senior contact for trading counterparties, the firms Evernorth transacts with, and custodians that safeguard its assets.

Jeandesboz brings more than a decade of institutional trading and portfolio management experience across digital and traditional markets. At Coinbase Asset Management, he served as co-chief investment officer and led tailored institutional strategies. Previously, he was lead derivatives trader at crypto exchange Coinbase (Nasdaq: COIN), overseeing options, futures, and blockchain-based markets. Earlier roles included interest rate derivatives trading at HSBC and quantitative strategy at Societe Generale, using mathematical models and data to guide trading decisions.

473 Million XRP Supports an Active Treasury Model

Evernorth’s completed merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9 brought its XRP treasury into public markets. Armada was a special purpose acquisition company formed to take another business public. Evernorth reported approximately 473 million XRP and about $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses. Institutional and digital asset investors included Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken, and GSR.

Investors gained access to the business through Evernorth’s Nasdaq trading debut under XRPN on Oct. 12, when its common stock began trading. Management intends to increase XRP per share through institutional and decentralized finance yield strategies, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities. XRP per share measures token holdings relative to outstanding stock, making share issuance relevant alongside asset growth.

Buying Evernorth stock provides ownership in a company whose results depend on treasury decisions, financing, and operating performance. Owning cryptocurrency directly instead gives the holder the digital asset itself.

Evernorth Eyes XRP Lending and DeFi Opportunities

Birla linked the appointment to opportunities involving tokenized real-world assets, digital representations of financial or physical assets, and decentralized finance. The XRP Ledger (XRPL) institutional lending framework outlined by Ripple would separate borrower assessment from blockchain execution: credit decisions would occur outside the ledger, while loan servicing and repayments would use it.

Separately, banking infrastructure around the network expanded Oct. 12 with Standard Chartered’s custody support for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger. The service safeguards eligible institutions’ Ripple USD tokens, a separate asset from XRP. Planned collateral integration with Ripple and LMAX Group would let eligible holdings support trading while remaining in bank custody, subject to testing, documentation, and approvals.

Jeandesboz also outlined his priorities for the business as it begins operating as a publicly traded company. He stated:

“The financial system is being rebuilt on programmable rails, and the XRP Ledger is becoming infrastructure where institutional capital can operate. Evernorth brings capital and public-market discipline to that shift at an early stage, and I look forward to building a treasury operation equal to the opportunity ahead.”

Alongside the appointment, Evernorth corrected the number of Class A shares issued to delayed-funding subscribers at closing. Evernorth reported 1,078,614 shares, replacing the 663,510 figure in its post-closing securities filing, which it attributed to a clerical error. The corrected issuance equaled the aggregate subscription amount, contributed in cash or XRP, divided by $10 per share.

title: Largest Philippines crypto exchange, Coins.ph, said to face central bank regulatory action
summary: The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, is said to have handled business transactions involving restricted offshore gaming and gambling companies.
content:
Oct 13, 2026, 9:00 p.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • The infractions, said to involve serving offshore gambling platforms, are serious enough to see the company stripped of its license to operate, according to one of the people.
  • Earlier this month, the central bank of the Philippines imposed restrictions on deposits through Coins.ph’s main wallet firm, according to people familiar with the process.
  • Several high-profile compliance staff left the exchange this year, including CCO Lexi Herrera and anti money-laundering specialists Chris Beaño and Irish Calagui.

Coins.ph, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the Philippines, is facing punitive action from financial regulators at the country’s central bank, two people with knowledge of the situation said.

The infractions, which are said to involve serving offshore gambling firms, are serious enough for the 12-year-old company to be stripped of its license to operate, which would cause “an earthquake” in the Philippines’ crypto ecosystem, according to one of the people.

The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, has a 24-hour spot trading volume of about $50 million and controls some 75%-80% of peso-to-stablecoin liquidity in the Philippines, a key transaction in the world's fourth-largest remittance recipient.

More than 10.8 million Filipinos live outside the country, according to the Commission on Filipinos Overseas, though most use banks and money transfer services to repatriate their earnings, some $43 billion a year.

At the start of this month, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) reportedly imposed restrictions on deposits to the exchange made through Coins.ph’s main wallet firm, DCPay Philippines.

The restrictions follow the departure of several high-profile compliance staffers, including chief compliance officer Lexi Herrera, the head of anti-money laundering (AML) transaction monitoring Chris Beaño and money laundering reporting officer Irish Calagui.

Neither Coins.ph nor the Philippines central bank responded to requests for comment by publication time.

A little over a year ago, the central bank clamped down on the use of e-wallet applications for gambling purposes, demanding institutions under its supervision cut in-app access to gambling sites.

As a result, several gambling entities migrated to Coins.ph, according to the people. The move had the added advantage of giving the firms access to crypto and stablecoins for paying offshore partners, according to a third person familiar with central bank regulatory processes.

The recent Coins.ph restriction was not time-bound, unlike the temporary suspensions typically imposed on market participants for failing to comply with throughput or latency requirements, for example. In this case, no reason was given, one of the people said.

Coins.ph was one of the earliest crypto wallets and exchanges in the Philippines and later pivoted to providing broader financial services.

In January 2019, Indonesian technology company Gojek bought Coins.ph for $95 million. Coins.ph was later sold to Wei Zhou, who was previously Binance’s chief financial officer.

title: Ripple’s $10M RLUSD Donation Could Help Generate $900M: Report
summary: Small business lending supported by Ripple’s RLUSD donation could help generate up to $900 million in GDP over a decade. The forecast connects a permanent capital contribution with borrowing, repeated loans, and economic activity across communities. Ripple’s $10 Million Lending Equity Gets a $900 Mi...
content:
Small business lending supported by Ripple’s RLUSD donation could help generate up to $900 million in GDP over a decade. The forecast connects a permanent capital contribution with borrowing, repeated loans, and economic activity across communities.

Key Takeaways

  • Ripple allocated $10 million of its $15 million gift to lending equity.
  • AOF projects the equity could produce roughly $156 million in small business lending.
  • The capital may attract up to $50 million from impact investors.

Ripple’s $10 Million Lending Equity Gets a $900 Million GDP Projection

Underserved small businesses could access financing backed by Ripple’s donation of Ripple USD (RLUSD). Jonathan Perri, social impact director at Ripple, highlighted the $900 million GDP projection on X on Oct. 12. Accion Opportunity Fund (AOF), a nonprofit small business lender, published the underlying findings on Oct. 8.

The $10 million lending allocation forms part of Ripple’s broader $15 million RLUSD donation to AOF in 2025. Its potential decade-long economic effects reflect capital that remains available to anchor borrowing over time. Perri wrote that the donation “could help generate as much as $900 million in new GDP over the next decade.” Gross domestic product (GDP) measures economic value added through production.

Perri’s earlier roughly $250 million output estimate assumed a $50 million loan pool and capital recycling about 2.5 times. It applied approximately $2 in annual economic output per dollar lent; the new model measures cumulative GDP over a decade.

How $10 Million Could Finance $156 Million in Loans

Permanent lending equity stays on AOF’s balance sheet, providing a financial foundation for borrowing from impact investors. Applying historical multipliers, ratios derived from AOF’s past funding and lending results, the study estimates Ripple’s $10 million allocation may attract as much as $50 million in new debt capital. Repayments allow that money to finance subsequent borrowers, potentially producing roughly $156 million in cumulative lending over the next decade.

Ripple funded the research, produced with TXP and ideas42, covering nearly 20,000 businesses and $960 million in loans. Researchers used the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis’ Regional Input-Output Modeling System, a model that estimates how activity in one industry affects the wider economy. Estimated historical results included $5.46 billion in GDP, more than 60,000 retained jobs, and over 10,000 new jobs.

The remaining $5 million of Ripple’s donation finances education, research, and a storytelling campaign, including its Digital Leap Forward Accelerator. The accelerator helps small business owners adopt digital tools and improve financial knowledge. Ripple’s original nonprofit funding commitment also included Hire Heroes USA, which assists veterans and military spouses with employment.

RLUSD Connects Digital Donations With Financial Infrastructure

The contribution was delivered in RLUSD, a digital token designed to maintain a value tied to the U.S. dollar. Such dollar-pegged stablecoins can transfer funds on blockchain networks, while AOF’s projected GDP comes from borrowing, repeated lending, and business activity. The $900 million estimate applies historical multipliers to the gift; actual future results will vary.

Ripple has also used RLUSD to finance education through nonprofit organizations distributing classroom resources across the United States. Its $25 million education commitment supported DonorsChoose and Teach For America, with most funding delivered in RLUSD. First-year results included 48,108 classroom projects funded through DonorsChoose across all 50 states.

Institutional services are expanding alongside those donations, with Standard Chartered launching RLUSD custody on the XRP Ledger on Oct. 12 through its branch in the Dubai International Financial Centre, a financial services hub in Dubai.

A separate planned collaboration with Ripple and LMAX Group, an operator of institutional trading venues, would allow eligible tokens to serve as trading collateral while remaining in bank custody. Collateral consists of assets pledged to secure trading obligations.

AOF plans a public discussion with its research partners and Ripple on Oct. 30 at 1 p.m. EDT.

title: Bitcoin Price Odds on Prediction Markets Give $100K Just 27%
summary: Bitcoin’s return to $100,000 is looking increasingly doubtful before 2027, at least in the eyes of prediction market traders. Polymarket assigns just a 27% probability to the milestone this year, while Kalshi’s October forecast sits at $87,000. With bitcoin trading near $83,416 on Tuesday, Oct. 13, ...
content:
Bitcoin’s return to $100,000 is looking increasingly doubtful before 2027, at least in the eyes of prediction market traders. Polymarket assigns just a 27% probability to the milestone this year, while Kalshi’s October forecast sits at $87,000. With bitcoin trading near $83,416 on Tuesday, Oct. 13, traders are pricing in a far greater chance of another retreat toward $80,000 than a spectacular six-figure comeback this month.

Key Takeaways

  • Polymarket traders give bitcoin just a 27% chance of hitting $100,000 before 2027, despite $75.1M in trading.
  • Kalshi’s October forecast sits at $87,000, while its year-end bitcoin projection stands at $83,554.
  • Polymarket bettors see a 57% chance of bitcoin touching $80,000 this October, versus 2% for $100,000.

Bitcoin’s $100K Comeback Faces a Skeptical Betting Crowd

Bitcoin’s six-figure price ambitions are getting a cold reception from prediction markets, where traders are putting real money behind decidedly modest expectations. On Oct. 13, Polymarket participants assigned just a 27% probability to bitcoin reaching $100,000 before 2027, while the odds of touching that milestone before November stood at a paltry 2%.

Meanwhile, Kalshi’s October forecast pointed toward $87,000, hardly the fireworks bullish investors might have anticipated. With bitcoin changing hands near $83,416, the betting crowd appears more concerned about defending $80,000 than reclaiming the cryptocurrency’s former six-figure territory.

Polymarket Traders Put $100K on the Back Burner

The numbers paint a sobering picture. The prediction marketplace Polymarket‘s 2026 bitcoin price market, which has attracted approximately $75.1 million in trading volume, gives bitcoin a 64% chance of reaching $90,000 before year’s end. At $95,000, confidence slips to 43%, while $100,000 commands just 27%. The odds deteriorate further at higher elevations, with $110,000 priced at 12% and $120,000 at 7%.

The downside isn’t getting a free pass, either. Traders assign a 37% probability to bitcoin touching $70,000 before 2027, while $65,000 carries 23% odds and $60,000 sits at 15%. These contracts measure whether bitcoin touches a specified price before expiration, not where it finishes the year. That’s an important distinction when interpreting the numbers.

October’s $80K Battleground Takes Center Stage

The shorter-term picture looks even less hospitable to bitcoin’s bulls. Polymarket’s October price market, with roughly $6.3 million in trading volume, assigns an 80% probability to bitcoin’s price touching $85,000 before November. However, the odds drop to 50% at $87,500, 32% at $90,000 and just 10% at $95,000.

Polymarket Bitcoin Price Odds for October 2026

Bitcoin Price TargetProbability
$87,500 ↑50%
$90,000 ↑32%
$100,000 ↑2%
$80,000 ↓57%
$75,000 ↓21%

BTC reference price: $83,416
Source: Polymarket at 6:45 p.m ET on Oct. 13
Expiration: Oct. 31, 2026

A return to $100,000 this month? Traders give that proposition a mere 2% chance. Meanwhile, bitcoin has a 57% implied probability of touching $80,000 and a 33% chance of sliding to $77,500. A retreat to $75,000 carries 21% odds. In other words, traders are assigning better odds to a $7,500 decline from the $83,416 reference price than to a $6,584 advance toward $90,000.

Kalshi’s $87K Forecast Throws Cold Water on the Bulls

Over at the prediction market Kalshi, the October bitcoin forecast stands at $87,000, down approximately $2,970 from its earlier reading. The platform’s $789,873 October event places the probability of bitcoin exceeding $87,500 at 49%, while $90,000 commands 35% and $92,500 attracts 22%.

Kalshi’s separate year-end market, which has recorded more than $41.3 million in volume, currently projects $83,554. It’s displayed settlement brackets assign 14% to a year-end finish between $80,000 and $84,999.99, compared with 12.7% for $85,000 to $89,999.99.

Six Figures Still Beckon, but the Clock Is Ticking

The longer-term betting crowd isn’t ready to bury bitcoin’s $100,000 ambitions. Polymarket’s milestone market assigns a 48% probability to bitcoin reaching six figures by March 31, 2027, rising to 58% by June and 70% by Dec. 31, 2027. Prediction market prices reflect traders’ collective expectations, not guarantees, and can change abruptly as new information arrives.

Still, the contradiction is striking. Traders give bitcoin a 70% chance of reaching $100,000 by the end of 2027, yet only a 27% chance before 2026 expires. The six-figure dream hasn’t received the ax, but the betting crowd appears increasingly willing to push its arrival into another calendar year.

title: Ledger asks resellers to halt sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong
summary: The wallet maker requested that devices be removed from shelves while investigators work to establish where tampering occurred.
content:
Ledger has requested sellers and distributors of its devices in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales and remove its hardware wallets from shelves as it investigates reports of tampered devices.

In a post on X on Tuesday, Ledger said the request covers resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.

“To be clear, as the investigation continues, the only confirmed incidents remain contained to Southeast Asia. We have not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere,” said Ledger.

“The investigation is ongoing to determine who tampered with these devices and where in the distribution chain it happened,” it added.

The wider sales suspension request expands on Ledger’s earlier request for reseller CryptoBilis to stop sales and shipments. The investigation became public on Oct. 9 after reports of stolen crypto linked to devices purchased through the reseller.

Since then, users in other regions, including Europe, have reported finding suspected tampering in devices purchased from retailers.

“We have no indication that Ledger’s infrastructure, systems or services or direct sales channel have been compromised,” the company said.

Related: Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports

title: Strive raising $500 million to buy additional bitcoin with new preferred share class
summary: SATS will offer a fixed 15% dividend yield at par and be junior to the company's existing SATA, which pays a variable rate (currently 13%).
content:
Resumen

  • Strive (ASST) is IPOing a new perpetual preferred stock, SATS, with a 15% fixed dividend.
  • The new share class will sit junior to the company’s existing perpetual preferred stock, SATA.
  • At closing of the IPO, Strive will set aside enough cash to fund 18 months of dividends on SATS.

Bitcoin treasury company Strive ASST$27,60·Mercado cerrado on Tuesday evening announced a new perpetual preferred stock, SATS, with a 15% fixed dividend.

The company is aiming to sell 5 million shares at $100 per share, for a capital raise of $500 million, with proceeds to be used to purchase additional bitcoin BTC$83.308,26, acquire income-producing assets, or buy back stock.

The new share class will sit junior to Strive’s current perpetual preferred, SATA, which has a variable rate (currently 13%).

Like SATA, SATS will pay dividends on a daily basis.

At closing of the offering, the company intends to establish a dividend reserve equal to the first 18 months of dividend payments on SATS.


Unlike most bitcoin treasury companies, including far larger peer Strategy, Strive has in recent weeks been able to significantly increase its bitcoin holdings.

The company last week acquired 3,311 bitcoin, bringing total holdings to 32,773 coins, currently worth about $2.7 billiion. Three months ago, holdings were below 20,000 coins.

title: Kraken Parent Payward Wins Full Dubai License, Plans UAE Launch
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Kraken Parent Payward Wins Full Dubai License, Plans UAE Launch
Kraken currently has more than 100 licenses and registrations worldwide. 
This post Kraken Parent Payward Wins Full Dubai License, Plans UAE Launch first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo.
content:
Crypto exchange Kraken’s parent company Payward has said it has plans to launch in the United Arab Emirates. 

After receiving full market approval from Dubai’s Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority, Payward said Tuesday that Payward can now operate as a regulated virtual asset service provider serving retail, professional and institutional investors. 

It follows a preliminary approval in May that allowed the company to complete its operational set-up ahead of onboarding clients.

At launch, Kraken clients in the UAE will be able to trade spot and margin with dirham-denominated pairs and fund and withdraw directly in dirhams. 

They’ll also have access to on-chain staking, xStocks tokenized equities and Krak for crypto transfers, while institutional clients gain OTC spot trading and Kraken Prime. Crypto derivatives and new yield products are expected later in 2026 and into 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

Payward holds more than 100 licenses and registrations worldwide, spanning Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.

The expansion comes as the company increasingly makes a number of deals. In September, Bloomberg reported that Nasdaq Inc. was investing $100 million in Payward in a deal valuing the company at $21 billion. Kraken will distribute Nasdaq’s tokenized stocks on its own platform, according to the report.

Payward and SoFi Technologies also recently announced a deal to route SoFi customers’ crypto orders through Kraken Prime, Kraken’s prime brokerage arm launched in 2025, and to list SoFi’s stablecoin on the exchange.

Kraken, like other crypto exchanges, is pushing into the traditional finance world, allowing users to trade stocks, bonds and other assets. The company has sold its app as a “primary account for everything.”

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Researchers Build First Working Post-Quantum Defense for Bitcoin’s Lightning Network
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Build First Working Post-Quantum Defense for Bitcoin’s Lightning Network
Second-layer solutions like Lightning may also need protection from quantum computers. Here’s how a research team appears to have cracked it. 
This post Researchers Build First Working Post-Quantum...
content:
Whether or not quantum computers will break Bitcoin one day is a hot topic. 

But what about second-layer solutions like Lightning? 

Well, researchers from East Texas A&M University, North American University, Florida Gulf Coast University, and Florida Institute of Technology have been working on that. 

In an announcement Tuesday, the team of researchers said that they built what they describe as the first full post-quantum security design for the Lightning Network.

As first uncovered in a research paper in September, the team said they added post-quantum cryptography to Lightning’s communications, payment requests and related systems, implemented in Rust-Lightning. 

It works like this: The solution layers new quantum-resistant cryptography on top of Lightning’s existing cryptography rather than replacing it. It uses ML-DSA digital signatures and ML-KEM key exchange, post-quantum algorithms standardized by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, alongside the classical methods Lightning already relies on. 

In this hybrid design, an attacker would have to break both the new and the old cryptography to compromise a connection or forge a payment request.

According to the team led by Dr. Ahmet Kurt, an assistant professor in East Texas A&M’s Department of Computer Science and Information Systems, it took about three to four months and roughly 11,000 lines of code — and it’s a complete working implementation, not just a small demo.

Lightning lets users make fast, cheap Bitcoin payments through a network of off-chain channels instead of recording each one on the blockchain. 

Its cryptography could eventually be broken by powerful quantum computers, and that risk exists even if Bitcoin itself gets upgraded, because Lightning has its own communication and payment systems, the team said. 

They added that their work demonstrates that Lightning’s off-chain systems can begin preparing for the quantum era independently while others focus on solutions for the mainnet. 

Quantum researchers have warned that a time will come when Bitcoin’s software — which underpins the biggest and strongest computer network in the world — will need to be upgraded to deal with quantum computing. 

While some crypto VC firms have urged action, top developers in the space have argued that many of today’s quantum computers have limited capabilities.

Still, they have noted that their development could arrive unexpectedly — just like advances with artificial intelligence — and have started developing some solutions, including top Bitcoin infrastructure firm, Blockstream. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: BNY Brings 24/7 Dollar Settlement to Singapore Gulf Bank
summary: Singapore Gulf Bank has expanded round-the-clock U.S. dollar settlement through BNY, allowing eligible payments to clear during weekends and U.S. public holidays. For crypto markets, the move is notable because traditional banks are beginning to offer one of the features that made stablecoins compel...
content:
Singapore Gulf Bank has expanded round-the-clock U.S. dollar settlement through BNY, allowing eligible payments to clear during weekends and U.S. public holidays. For crypto markets, the move is notable because traditional banks are beginning to offer one of the features that made stablecoins compelling: dollars that move beyond banking hours.

Key Takeaways

  • Singapore Gulf Bank adopted BNY’s 24/7 USD settlement for eligible weekend and holiday payments.
  • The move narrows stablecoins’ always-on edge as banks extend dollar settlement beyond normal hours.
  • Attention now shifts to whether banks can match crypto on speed, reach, and programmability.

BNY Pushes Traditional Banking Closer to Crypto’s 24/7 Model

Traditional finance is starting to chip away at crypto’s monopoly on always-on money.

Singapore Gulf Bank said it has adopted BNY’s 24/7 USD Book Transfers service, giving eligible corporate and retail clients the ability to settle qualifying dollar payments outside standard U.S. banking hours.

That includes weekends and U.S. public holidays.

The service can be used for account funding, corporate payables, and time-sensitive cross-border treasury transactions. Singapore Gulf Bank said it is among the first financial institutions globally to adopt the system.

Dollar Settlement Moves Beyond the Banking Clock

The service allows USD transfers to settle at any time between eligible accounts held directly with BNY or through correspondent banks enrolled in the network.

That matters for companies operating across multiple time zones, where waiting for U.S. banking hours can create liquidity and settlement delays.

“Our clients operate across markets and time zones, and their business needs do not always fall within traditional U.S. banking hours,” SGB Executive Vice Chairman Ali Moosa said.

For treasury teams in the Gulf, Asia, and other international markets, removing those time restrictions could simplify cross-border cash management.

Traditional Finance Borrows From the Crypto Playbook

The development also has clear implications for crypto and stablecoins.

One of the strongest arguments for dollar-backed stablecoins such as USDC and USDT has been their ability to move globally at any hour, while conventional banking infrastructure often pauses overnight or during weekends.

BNY’s system does not replicate permissionless blockchain settlement. Transfers remain limited to eligible institutions and accounts within its participating banking network.

Still, 24/7 settlement reduces part of the operational gap.

As banks modernize payment infrastructure, stablecoins may increasingly compete on programmability, global accessibility, and onchain integration rather than simply being available around the clock.

Cross-Border Treasury Is Becoming an Always-on Market

BNY said continuous settlement can give institutions more flexibility in managing liquidity.

“Round-the-clock USD settlement gives institutions greater agility in managing liquidity and fulfilling urgent financial obligations,” said Bana Akkad Azhari, EMEA head of global payments and trade at BNY.

That is increasingly important as financial markets move toward faster settlement and crypto markets operate continuously. For Singapore Gulf Bank, the integration expands its correspondent banking network across the Gulf, Asia, and other markets.

For the broader financial industry, the signal is bigger.

Always-on settlement is no longer solely a crypto feature. Banks are starting to bring it into conventional dollar infrastructure, and that could reshape where stablecoins maintain their strongest competitive advantage.

title: BNY, Citadel Securities test tokenized U.S. Treasuries to speed up Wall Street financing
summary: The transaction shows how blockchain-based government bonds could help trading firms move collateral faster between settlement and financing.
content:
Oct 13, 2026, 5:52 p.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • BNY and Citadel Securities completed a transaction showing how tokenized U.S. Treasuries can move from settlement into financing.
  • The effort targets a key bottleneck in financial markets: moving government bonds used as collateral for trading and borrowing.
  • BNY plans to expand digital cash services and traditional settlement hours as it works toward around-the-clock markets.

BNY, the world’s largest custody bank, and trading giant Citadel Securities said Tuesday they had completed a transaction using tokenized U.S. Treasuries, showing how blockchain technology could help Wall Street move assets between trading and financing more quickly.

The transfer focused on collateral, a key part of financial markets. Banks and trading firms use U.S. government bonds to secure short-term loans and fund trading activity. Moving those bonds between accounts and settlement systems can take time, tying up assets that could otherwise be put to work.

The effort comes as Wall Street explores bringing traditional assets onto blockchains. Firms including BlackRock, Franklin Templeton and JPMorgan have embraced tokenized funds and securities, betting the technology can shorten settlement times, automate processes and make assets easier to move.

Putting tokenized Treasuries to work

The aim of the BNY-Citadel Securities transaction was to demonstrate how tokenized government bonds could move from settlement into financing, potentially allowing firms to reuse collateral sooner and free up cash for other trades.

“Efficient movement of high-quality collateral is fundamental to well-functioning markets,” said Dan Doherty, digital assets operations lead at Citadel Securities, in a statement. He added that reducing delays across the trade lifecycle could improve how institutional markets operate.

BNY said it plans to introduce more digital cash and tokenized deposit capabilities to support blockchain-based settlement and financing.

Meanwhile, the bank said it expects to extend the operating hours of its traditional settlement systems for Federal Reserve-eligible securities and U.S. triparty transactions, aiming to reach European and Asian trading hours next year. Triparty transactions are a form of short-term financing in which a bank manages collateral between borrowers and lenders.

“By using a tokenized representation of a U.S. Treasury across both settlement and financing, we are enabling more connected, efficient and always-on financial system,” said Carolyn Weinberg, chief innovation and market transformation officer at BNY, in a statement.

title: Ethereum NFT Marketplace Blur to Shutter After Trading Volume Vanishes
summary: Once the largest Ethereum NFT marketplace around, Blur said this week that it will shut off its frontend in November, concluding its run as recent trading volume sat at a fraction of its previous peaks. Blur’s Impending Demise Follows Domination Blur’s “frontend will be deprecated on Nov. 12, 2026,”...
content:
Once the largest Ethereum NFT marketplace around, Blur said this week that it will shut off its frontend in November, concluding its run as recent trading volume sat at a fraction of its previous peaks.

Key Takeaways

  • Ethereum NFT marketplace Blur will shut down its website on Nov. 12, 2026.
  • Blur’s lending protocol Blend will also stop facilitating loans on the same date.
  • The NFT market has cooled dramatically in the last few years, and trading volume on the marketplace has collapsed since its early 2023 peak.

Blur’s Impending Demise Follows Domination

Blur’s “frontend will be deprecated on Nov. 12, 2026,” according to a Monday post on X, meaning that the marketplace website will no longer be available for traders. The underlying trading protocol will continue to function and can be accessed via smart contract interactions and aggregators, but the branded Blur marketplace will cease to exist this time next month.

Furthermore, Blur’s NFT-backed lending protocol, Blend, will stop facilitating loans on the same date, per an X post. “Borrowers have until then to repay their loans or allow them to default,” it reads. “After this date, we will provide a frontend tool to help users withdraw their assets from Blend.”

Blur launched in late 2022 after the NFT bull market of 2021 and early 2022 was already losing steam, but it shook up the space early the following year by overtaking the dominant rival marketplace, Opensea. That move was fueled in large part by offering traders a share of a BLUR token airdrop, prompting billions of dollars’ worth of Ethereum NFT trades.

However, Blur’s rise was controversial among NFT enthusiasts. While the airdrop amounted to a giveaway of free crypto cash for users, some collectors believed the resulting avalanche of rapid trading devalued the non-fungible assets, with some analysts labeling the trading volume as “wash trading.”

Blur defended its model to Decrypt in 2023, saying the volume surge was “misunderstood” by some analysts. But as NFT prices broadly continued to sink, the platform continued to take heat from pockets of the industry. Early momentum on Blur cooled significantly as the appeal of token incentives faded with the falling price of BLUR, however.

Over the last year, data from Token Terminal shows Opensea back on top with $557 million worth of NFT trading volume, compared to $235 million for Blur. Per the same data resource, Blur’s trading volume across all of September tallied $19.15 million, compared to a peak month of nearly $1.43 billion back in March 2023.

While Blur’s relevance as a prominent NFT marketplace has faded in recent years, some of the hard feelings still linger among collectors. “Good riddance. You destroyed NFTs. Please shut down and never come back,” one X user replied to the post. Another suggested that Blur’s exit would be the “bottom signal for NFTs.”

Earlier this month, Blur founder Tieshun “Pacman” Roquerre announced that Blast—an Ethereum Layer 2 network launched in 2024—would also shut down, with plans to take the network offline on October 26. Another Layer 2 network, Abstract, is set to close down in December.

Blur isn’t the only marketplace to shut down in 2026 as NFT demand remains diminished. Once-prominent platforms Nifty Gateway and Foundation both shuttered this year, while former top marketplace Magic Eden significantly scaled back support amid a pivot towards gambling.

The price of BLUR fell to a new low on Tuesday, crashing 35% in the last 24 hours to $0.0115—down 99.8% from its all-time high above $5.00.

title: Benzinga and WNSTN Pitch Turnkey AI to Brokers With Promise of 2.3x Trading Boost
summary:

The service brings together Benzinga...

2026-10-13T23:01:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 21:01 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Brokers can add portfolio-aware market answers to their own platforms through an API or white-label interface.
  • WNSTN says its compliance agent checks every response, but brokers will still need to supervise the personalised answers their clients receive.

Financial data vendor Benzinga and AI developer WNSTN have rolled out a white-label conversational assistant designed to turn market research into instant client order flow inside third-party brokerage apps, promising to more than double retail trading frequency.

The service brings together Benzinga’s market information and WNSTN’s conversational technology. Brokers can integrate it into their existing platforms through an API or deploy it as a white-label product.

The companies first announced their partnership in June 2025. WNSTN’s technology subsequently powered natural-language chat, news summaries and market analysis inside Benzinga Pro, as well as localised conversations on Benzinga’s international websites.

The new offering adapts that integration for external brokerage clients.

Data and Personalisation in One Broker Interface

Benzinga supplies the information behind the AI assistant, including financial news, analyst ratings, earnings information, regulatory filings and corporate events. Its datasets also explain movements in share prices.

WNSTN turns that information into a conversational service. The assistant can adapt responses and summaries to a customer’s portfolio, monitor relevant market developments and surface investment ideas without requiring the user to leave the broker’s platform.

The company presents increased customer activity as a central benefit of this model. Its case study covers more than 88,000 trades at an unnamed US broker-dealer over approximately 12 months.

The company divided customers into non-users, people who interacted with the assistant once and active users who returned to it.

After removing outliers, WNSTN found that active users, those who engaged with the assistant more than once, made 2.3 times as many trades per day at the median as customers who did not use it. WNSTN also says that roughly half of users who chatted with the assistant placed a trade within 24 hours.

What Brokers Must Supervise

Because the assistant’s answers may reflect a customer’s portfolio and prompt investment actions, brokers need to be particularly careful as responses may be read as a personal recommendation.

WNSTN says every response passes through a separate Compliance Officer agent trained on US and European regulatory requirements.

However, that check does not guarantee that every answer will be accurate or compliant. Brokers will judge the offering by whether it keeps clients engaged and whether they can reliably supervise what it tells them.

title: Ripple Teams With Stripe-Owned Privy to Bring Wallet Tech to XRP Ledger
summary: Ripple has partnered with cryptocurrency wallet infrastructure provider Privy to expand payment capabilities on the XRP Ledger (XRPL), giving developers new tools to build stablecoin applications and automated financial transactions powered by AI. XRPL Gets Privy to Stripe’s Wallet Tech The collabor...
content:
Ripple has partnered with cryptocurrency wallet infrastructure provider Privy to expand payment capabilities on the XRP Ledger (XRPL), giving developers new tools to build stablecoin applications and automated financial transactions powered by AI.

Key Takeaways

  • Ripple and Privy partnered to expand wallet infrastructure and payment capabilities on the XRP Ledger.
  • The integration enables autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to conduct transactions using XRP, RLUSD, and other digital assets.
  • Privy simplifies wallet management, with plans to add transaction controls and gas sponsorship.

XRPL Gets Privy to Stripe’s Wallet Tech

The collaboration, announced Tuesday by Privy, will allow developers to create and manage XRPL wallets programmatically, sign transactions, and build applications using XRP, Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin, and other digital assets supported by the network.

The integration is designed to simplify wallet management for fintech companies and payment providers, allowing them to embed cryptocurrency functionality directly into their products without requiring customers to manage private keys.

A central focus is agentic commerce, an emerging category of financial activity in which autonomous AI agents can initiate payments and conduct transactions on behalf of users.

Privy’s server-side wallet infrastructure will enable AI agents to hold and transfer digital assets, including through the x402 payment protocol, which supports automated payments between software applications and online services.

“Privy brings proven wallet infrastructure that makes it easier for fintechs and developers to bring XRPL into real products, from payments and stablecoin experiences to emerging forms of agentic commerce,” said Markus Infanger, senior vice president of RippleX at Ripple, in a statement.

The companies highlighted XRPL’s established payments infrastructure, including fast settlement speeds, low transaction costs and support for tokenized real-world assets. According to Privy, the blockchain has accumulated more than 8 million funded accounts and processed over $1 trillion in value during its 14-year history.

Developers will also be able to offer users wallet ownership and portability through private key and seed phrase exports. Privy said it plans to expand the integration with additional capabilities, including transaction policy controls and gas sponsorship, which would give developers greater oversight of automated transactions while reducing complexity for end users.

“Stablecoins are changing how money moves, and XRPL has been building for payments from the start,” said Privy co-founder and CEO Henri Stern, in a statement. “We’re excited to make Privy wallets available to developers building on XRPL, from global payments to agentic commerce, and whatever comes next.”

title: Bitcoin Price Defends $81.5K ETF Cost Basis Despite Rising Outflows
summary: Bitcoin has twice defended the roughly $81,500 cost basis of U.S. spot ETF investors, even after $681 million in net ETF outflows last week and another $65 million shed on Monday. Glassnode Flags $77.5K if Bitcoin Loses ETF Cost Basis Bitcoin is testing whether institutional ownership has permanentl...
content:
Bitcoin has twice defended the roughly $81,500 cost basis of U.S. spot ETF investors, even after $681 million in net ETF outflows last week and another $65 million shed on Monday.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin twice defended the $81.5K ETF cost basis despite $746M in recent fund outflows.
  • Glassnode sees $77.5K as the next major support if institutional demand fails to hold the floor.
  • ETF investor positioning now matters more than fresh inflows for bitcoin’s next move.

Glassnode Flags $77.5K if Bitcoin Loses ETF Cost Basis

Bitcoin is testing whether institutional ownership has permanently changed the character of its market.

The cryptocurrency has bounced twice from roughly $81,500, a level Glassnode identifies as the aggregate cost basis for U.S. spot bitcoin ETF investors. That matters because BTC spent much of this year below the threshold, while its May rally stalled just underneath it.

What was once resistance is now acting as support.

More strikingly, bitcoin has defended the level despite $681 million in net U.S. spot ETF outflows last week and another $65 million outflow on Monday. If support eventually breaks, then Glassnode points to the true market mean near $77,500 as the next major level.

ETF Cost Basis Becomes Bitcoin’s New Line in the Sand

The resilience around $81,500 is notable because ETF flows have recently been working against bitcoin rather than supporting it. Vugar Usi Zade, CEO of MEXC, argued that institutional capital has nevertheless created a stronger structural floor.

“Bitcoin is moving into a phase of institutional maturity, where the $80,000 mark has become the average cost for positions held by spot ETFs and custodial services,” he said.

If major funds accumulated heavily around this zone, then declines toward $80,000 may increasingly attract buyers rather than trigger panic.

Bitcoin Is Also Outrunning Broader Liquidity

Institutional positioning is not the only constructive signal.

Bitcoin Magazine analysis comparing BTC with Federal Reserve net liquidity noted that bitcoin has recently outperformed the broader liquidity backdrop, even while maintaining a meaningful longer-term relationship with it. That is important because bitcoin has historically been highly sensitive to liquidity conditions.

Recent performance suggests investor demand may be contributing more to bitcoin’s price action, rather than simply rising and falling with shifts in macro liquidity. Still, BTC remains exposed to broader financial conditions. Liquidity matters, even if it is no longer the only force driving the market.

$77.5K Becomes the Risk Level to Watch

Two successful defenses of the ETF cost basis are encouraging. Defending it while ETFs are recording net redemptions is an even stronger test. However, the $81,500 mark is not guaranteed to hold. Continued ETF withdrawals could eventually overwhelm underlying spot demand.

For traders, the setup is increasingly clear.

Bitcoin’s price holding above $81,500 despite persistent outflows would reinforce the argument that institutional positioning has created a new BTC floor. Losing it would quickly shift attention toward $77,500.

The key question is no longer whether ETFs can push bitcoin higher. It is whether bitcoin can hold the ETF cost basis while money is leaving the funds.

title: IG Group Alumni Raise $1.2 Million for AI Search Startup
summary:
Obsero, founded by former IG Group marketers Michael Logue and Andy Francos, has raised $1.2 million to develop a platform that measures how brands appear in answers produced by ChatGPT and other AI search tools. 
SFC Capital led the seed round 13 months after the London startup was established in S...
content:
2026-10-13T21:50:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 19:50 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The startup tracks whether brands appear in AI-generated answers, how they are presented and which external sources influence those responses.
  • It already works with Pepperstone and other financial companies as brokers begin assessing AI search as a potential customer-discovery channel.

Obsero, founded by former IG Group marketers Michael Logue and Andy Francos, has raised $1.2 million to develop a platform that measures how brands appear in answers produced by ChatGPT and other AI search tools.

SFC Capital led the seed round 13 months after the London startup was established in September 2025. Angel investors and several Obsero customers also participated, although the company did not identify the participating customers.

From IG Group to AI Search

The founders’ backgrounds help explain why Obsero is gaining traction among brokers and other consumer-facing financial companies.

Logue spent more than 13 years across two periods at IG and IG Group, most recently as Product and Marketing Director for its international business. Between those periods, he served as VP of Growth at tastytrade.

Francos has two decades of organic-search experience, including positions at IG, P&G and Cazoo. He said Cazoo attributed £252 million in revenue to organic search during his tenure.

Obsero applies that client-side marketing experience to the shift from conventional search results towards AI-generated answers.

How Obsero Tracks AI Recommendations

The platform models customer questions and collects responses from ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Mode. It then measures whether a brand appears, how prominently it is presented, the tone of the answer and which publishers or websites are cited.

Obsero founders say they analysed more than 10 million AI responses during its first year. The funding will support the development of specialised AI agents that turn knowledge from its consulting work into tools for marketing teams.

The company also plans to more than double its engineering workforce and expand its commercial operations.

Why Brokers Are Paying Attention

Named customers include Zopa, Pepperstone and Zoopla. Obsero also says it works with other brokers and fintech startups, although their names are not disclosed.

A J.D. Power study found that 51% of surveyed consumers had used AI for financial information or advice. Investing and stock-market questions were among the most common subjects, giving brokers a reason to monitor whether their brands appear when users compare platforms or research products.

That does not yet establish AI answers as a major acquisition channel for brokers. Obsero’s next test is whether financial companies begin treating visibility in those answers as a recurring marketing expense.

title: Most tokenized stock trading on Solana, BNB Chain occurs outside US market hours
summary: Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.
content:
Most trading in tokenized stocks on major blockchains now takes place outside regular US market hours, offering an early indication that around-the-clock trading could be one of the biggest advantages of putting equities onchain.

According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4 pm Eastern trading session. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.

Meanwhile, Jupiter, a major Solana-based trading platform, reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume.

Source: The Kobeissi Letter

The figures suggest investors use tokenized stocks to trade when traditional US exchanges are closed, rather than simply replicating activity during regular market hours. 

The growth comes as tokenized stock values have increased by 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion, according to RWA.xyz data. A significant portion of that value is concentrated among issuers such as Ondo Global Markets, xStocks and bStocks, whose tokens are issued and traded across different blockchains.

Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules

Wall Street moves toward onchain stock trading

The growth in round-the-clock trading comes as US regulators begin opening the door to tokenized equities in traditional markets. Last month, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced an “innovation exemption” allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains.

SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda said participating venues must publish transaction data in US dollars, including trade prices, sizes, timestamps and daily trading volumes. They must also disclose liquidity pool addresses and balances.

Unlike existing tokenized stock products such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets, which are generally unavailable to US investors, the SEC exemption allows qualifying venues to offer tokenized US equities domestically, provided they preserve shareholder rights and meet trading and disclosure requirements.

Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

title: Ledger Spy Implant Scandal Prompts Mediamarkt Sales Freeze
summary: On Oct. 13, the hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger revealed new details about how criminals tampered with its hardware wallets and potentially stole customers’ cryptocurrency. The firm also noted that major European electronics retailer Mediamarkt Saturn has temporarily stopped selling Ledger devic...
content:
On Oct. 13, the hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger revealed new details about how criminals tampered with its hardware wallets and potentially stole customers’ cryptocurrency. The firm also noted that major European electronics retailer Mediamarkt Saturn has temporarily stopped selling Ledger devices.

Key Takeaways

  • Ledger investigators discovered that attackers secretly installed hardware implants capable of capturing customers’ 24-word recovery phrases and transmitting them over cellular networks.
  • Estimated reported losses have climbed from $86 million to $93 million, but Ledger says the figures remain unverified and confirmed losses involve devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller Cryptobilis.
  • European retailer Mediamarkt Saturn has suspended Ledger sales following a separate tampering report in Germany, while rival Trezor is tightening its reseller network amid growing supply chain security concerns.

Ledger Investigation Uncovers Hidden Device That Steals Recovery Phrases

Ledger has been dealing with a catastrophic issue after reports noted that funds were being siphoned from its devices on Oct. 9, 2026. Initially, reports detailed that projected losses amounted to around $86 million, but estimates have since increased to $93 million. Four days later, Ledger has taken to X to explain how its investigation centers on devices sold by Cryptobilis, a reseller operating in Southeast Asia.

The announcement on Tuesday explains that the most important discovery is that the attackers installed a tiny spying device inside the Ledger wallet itself. This device could secretly read a customer’s 24-word recovery phrase and transmit it to the attackers over a cellular network. According to Ledger’s security research team, known as Donjon, the attack involved several steps.

“Based on the Donjon’s analysis of the attack, the implant sits inside the enclosure and reads the data shown on the screen,” Ledger said. “During setup, the signer displays the 24-word recovery phrase. When the implant detects these screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM.”

The company continued:

“The implant is a separate component. It does not modify the Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, and it does not alter transactions or signatures.”

All confirmed fund losses associated with the incident disclosed on Oct. 9 involve wallets purchased through Cryptobilis, the wallet maker said. “We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost,” Ledger explained, noting that estimates like the recent $93 million are “not fully verified.”

Ledger is urging anyone who purchased a wallet from Cryptobilis to take precautions. Customers who haven’t activated their devices should avoid setting them up, the company insisted.

Mediamarkt Halts Ledger Sales as Tampering Allegations Spread

In another update, Ledger also said that another reseller, Mediamarkt Saturn, has temporarily stopped selling Ledger hardware wallets. “The sale of Ledger devices in their stores and online while the investigation continues,” the company explained.

Ledger’s announcement concerning Mediamarkt follows a wave of allegations circulating on X, where several accounts claim that Ledger hardware wallets purchased from the European retailer had been physically tampered with.

Ledger said the Mediamarkt pause followed a “report of an implant from one customer in Germany,” but further stressed that “no loss of funds were reported.” The company’s latest statement offered little in the way of substantive clarification, leaving public concerns largely unresolved as speculation and waves of reports continue to circulate across social media. The firm’s competitor Trezor also announced on Tuesday that it was scaling back its resale partners in the wake of Ledger’s incident.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports of tampered Ledger wallets, MediaMarktSaturn pulled Ledger products from stores and online platforms and Aptos launched an encrypted transaction feature to protect traders from frontrunning and sandwich attacks.

Trezor cuts reseller network after Ledger wallet tampering reports

Hardware wallet maker Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports that a Southeast Asian reseller modified Ledger devices to steal users’ recovery phrases.

Trezor said Tuesday the decision was precautionary and that it had no evidence its own devices were compromised. Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders said affected resellers would lose their authorized status on Jan. 1, with shipments to those businesses stopping immediately.

The move follows rival Ledger’s confirmation that at least one device sold by reseller CryptoBilis contained an unauthorized hardware implant capable of capturing recovery phrases and transmitting them over cellular networks.

The incident has raised questions about the security of hardware wallet supply chains. Trezor told Cointelegraph that its existing checks can detect counterfeit devices and modified firmware, but the Ledger implant operated differently by reading information displayed on the device’s screen.

Blockchain investigators have estimated potential losses of between $72 million and $86 million, although Ledger said it had not confirmed the total.

Trezor advised customers to purchase devices directly from the manufacturer and consider multisignature wallets using hardware from different providers.

MediaMarktSaturn pulls Ledger products amid tampering reports

MediaMarktSaturn, the parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt, has removed Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms amid reports of tampered hardware wallets.

“The products have been removed from our product lineup internationally in all of our countries. We did this as a precautionary measure,” a MediaMarktSaturn spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

Ledger said Tuesday that MediaMarktSaturn suspended sales in coordination with the wallet maker following a report of a hardware implant from a customer in Germany. Ledger said no fund losses had been reported in connection with that case and that it had no indication its infrastructure, systems or services were compromised.

An X user known as Johannes claimed Monday that he purchased two Ledger wallets from separate MediaMarkt stores. He said both contained unauthorized cables and cellular modules.

The security concerns emerged Friday after Ledger said it is investigating reports of losses involving devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger said Tuesday that implants transmitted users’ recovery phrases over cellular networks and that it was investigating reports beyond CryptoBilis.

Aptos rolls out Encrypted Mempool to curb frontrunning, sandwich attacks

Layer-1 blockchain Aptos has launched an optional new feature that could help shield traders from attacks involving maximal extractable value (MEV), including frontrunning and sandwich attacks. 

On Monday, Aptos said its Encrypted Mempool feature is now live on its mainnet, allowing users to opt in to keep pending transactions encrypted until their block ordering is finalized. Aptos said the feature was built for institutions submitting large transactions to the chain, traders wanting to avoid MEV risk, AI agents and builders. 

“When you send a transaction on any major chain today, anyone watching the network can see the details before it executes, the function you’re calling, the assets and amounts involved, and the contracts you’re interacting with,” Aptos said. “Bots use that visibility to trade against you or copy your strategy.”  

Sandwich attacks, one form of MEV attack, cost Ethereum traders about $60 million over the 12 months through October 2025, according to Cointelegraph’s analysis of EigenPhi data. On Solana, sandwich attacks generated $29.7 million for bots over an 11-month period examined by Bitquery, which identified nearly 6.9 million attacks affecting about 2.2 million wallets.

title: Russia Adds Sberbank to Crypto Exchange Register, Joining 9 Firms Before Dec. 1 Launch
summary:
Key Takeaways: The Central Bank of Russia has granted Sberbank permission to provide cryptocurrency exchange. Nine companies were added to the country’s register of crypto exchanges, including VTB and T-Invest
The post Russia Adds Sberbank to Crypto Exchange Register, Joining 9 Firms Before Dec. 1 L...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Central Bank of Russia has granted Sberbank permission to provide cryptocurrency exchange.
  • Nine companies were added to the country’s register of crypto exchanges, including VTB and T-Invest Lab.
  • On December 1, 2026, Sberbank will offer its first crypto products on its existing customer platforms.

Russia has extended its regulated crypto market by placing Sberbank on the list of the Bank of Russia of organizations based in the country that are permitted to exchange cryptocurrencies.

Approval will enable the world’s largest lender to have a more formal position in the crypto sphere after also being placed in Russia’s digital depository register earlier this month. 

Read More: Sberbank’s Crypto Lending Push Targets Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT Collateral

  • Sberbank Gets Approval to Offer Crypto Exchange Services
  • Sberbank Also Secures Digital Depository Status
    • Russia Opens Regulated Crypto Infrastructure to Banks
    • Dec. 1 Could Mark a Bigger Crypto Expansion

Sberbank Gets Approval to Offer Crypto Exchange Services

On October 12, the Bank of Russia included Sberbank in its list of crypto exchange organizations. Under Russia’s new regulatory framework, the registration will enable the bank to deliver services related to digital currency circulation and exchange.

Sberbank is to create its first crypto products by December 1 and make them available in existing interfaces for the user. That could help people who already use banking services to continue using them, without migrating to a separate crypto-native platform.

The latest one makes Russia the top country for crypto exchange operations with a total of nine. Other accredited firms include T-Invest Lab, part of the T-Technologies group together with T-Bank.

Sberbank Also Secures Digital Depository Status

The exchange was added to Russia’s digital depository register earlier this month, which is why it is included on Sberbank’s list of exchanges. There are different functions shipped with the two registrations.

Crypto exchange operators can provide services for buying and selling digital currencies, whereas digital depositories can be used to record crypto asset ownership and transactions, along with related rights to digital currencies.

There are currently five organizations, VTB and Atomyze among them, in Russia’s depository register.

Russia Opens Regulated Crypto Infrastructure to Banks

The registrations follow the introduction of Russia’s broader legal framework for digital currencies and digital rights, which took effect on September 1.

Under the framework, crypto transactions can use existing financial-market infrastructure, including brokers, exchanges and trustees, alongside newly authorized crypto exchanges and digital depositories.

Banks and other eligible organizations have been able to apply for the required registrations since October 5. Some established financial institutions can use a simplified notification process that may allow registration within one day.

Read More: Russia Busts 9 Illegal Crypto Exchanges in Moscow Over Ukraine-Linked Scam Funds

Dec. 1 Could Mark a Bigger Crypto Expansion

Sberbank is not alone when it comes to getting ready to launch crypto services in December. It’s coming as Russia is in the midst of creating a central bank-regulated framework for crypto trading, custody, and other digital-asset services.

As an exchange and depository bank, Sberbank would have the opportunity to offer its users access to a trading service next to its custody and ownership-record business in the financial market.

The upcoming launch in December will serve as a significant milestone in the company’s broadened use of cryptocurrency in customer platforms.

title: Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
summary: CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.
content:
Hardware wallet producer Trezor announced it would reduce its number of resellers as a “preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution,” following reports that malicious implants had been installed in devices made by competitor Ledger.

In a Tuesday X post, Trezor said there was “not a single piece of evidence that [its] devices have been compromised” after reports that Ledger hardware wallet users had found malicious implants that exposed recovery phrases. 

However, Trezor said that it would reduce the number of its resellers, citing “recent supply-chain incidents.” Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders added that he had notified certain resellers that they would be removed from the company’s list of authorized entities on Jan. 1, and would halt shipments of Trezor devices starting on Tuesday. 

Source: Trezor CCO Danny Sanders

Trezor’s response came just days after Ledger confirmed that at least one of its devices purchased by a Southeast Asian reseller contained an unauthorized hardware implant, potentially leading to millions of dollars in losses for users. The wallets, sold by reseller CryptoBilis, captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks.

“Our setup checks are built to catch counterfeit devices and modified firmware,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph. “The implant found in a device bought from CryptoBilis works differently. This is a unique way of tampering with the device, which doesn’t modify the firmware, but reads information on the screen and later sends it to the attacker. So far, we have not seen this specific type of attack on Trezor devices in the real world.” 

Related: Ledger investigates fund losses linked to Southeast Asian reseller, warns users

During the investigation, CryptoBilis, an authorized Trezor reseller, suspended all hardware wallet sales. The parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt also announced that it had removed all Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms “as a precautionary measure.”

How much in user funds was lost?

Blockchain sleuths are still investigating the extent of losses for hardware wallet users, but research from two individuals suggested between $72 million and $86 million. Ledger reported on Tuesday that it had “not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost” due to the breaches.

The Trezor spokesperson advised users to buy products directly from the company, “checking the seal is intact,” and consider a multisignature wallet “with devices from different makers, so one compromised device can’t move funds on its own.”

title: Interactive Brokers Adds Ether Staking with Fees Capped at 30% of Rewards
summary:
Eligible Interactive Brokers clients in the US can now stake Ether and earn blockchain rewards through the same portal they use to manage traditional investments. 
Zero Hash provides the staking service and holds the assets in an account opened in the customer’s name. Interactive Brokers provides ac...
content:
2026-10-13T20:00:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 18:00 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Ether rewards remain staked and can compound until the client requests to withdraw the assets; no fee applies if the stake generates no reward.
  • Zero Hash provides the service and holds the assets outside IBKR brokerage accounts, leaving them without SIPC protection.

Eligible Interactive Brokers clients in the US can now stake Ether and earn blockchain rewards through the same portal they use to manage traditional investments.

Zero Hash provides the staking service and holds the assets in an account opened in the customer’s name. Interactive Brokers provides access through its Client Portal but does not custody or stake the Ether itself.

Put your Ethereum to work. Eligible IBKR LLC clients can now stake ETH and earn crypto rewards through the IBKR platform. https://t.co/DWtk8PMxJJ https://t.co/9I9VVd3fyW

— Interactive Brokers (@IBKR) October 13, 2026

How Ether Staking Works

Clients choose how much Ether to stake through the IBKR Client Portal. Zero Hash then places the assets with Ethereum validators and credits any rewards back to the client’s staked balance, where they can continue compounding until the Ether is unstaked.

Interactive Brokers and Zero Hash deduct their fees from the rewards before crediting the remainder to the customer. Their combined charge is capped at 30%, and no fee applies if the stake earns nothing.

Neither the reward rate nor payment is guaranteed because both depend on Ethereum network conditions and validator performance.

Crypto Assets Remain Outside SIPC Protection

The split between the two providers also determines which protections apply.

Assets held in a customer’s Zero Hash account, including cryptocurrency and fiat balances, are not protected by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC) or the customer-protection rules covering securities in an Interactive Brokers brokerage account.

Customers also bear losses if problems occur at Zero Hash or during the staking process. These may result from validator penalties, known as slashing, or service disruptions that delay rewards or temporarily prevent assets from being staked or unstaked.

Staking Extends IBKR’s Crypto Offering

The launch extends a relationship that goes beyond a standard infrastructure contract. Interactive Brokers led Zero Hash’s $104 million funding round in 2025, when the crypto infrastructure provider was valued at $1 billion.

Zero Hash already supports several of the broker’s digital-asset services. Interactive Brokers introduced 24/7 account funding with stablecoins in January and later expanded crypto transfers and its selection to 20 assets. Ether staking adds another product to the same infrastructure relationship.

Robinhood, eToro and Trade Republic already offer staking in their respective markets. Interactive Brokers is now moving closer to that level of crypto functionality, while maintaining a clear division between its regulated brokerage business and the Zero Hash accounts that hold clients’ digital assets.

title: The Amount of Bitcoin on Exchanges Is Shrinking. Is a Rally Imminent?
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

The Amount of Bitcoin on Exchanges Is Shrinking. Is a Rally Imminent?
A CryptoQuant researcher has said that bitcoin’s supply dynamics could soon help its price.  
This post The Amount of Bitcoin on Exchanges Is Shrinking. Is a Rally Imminent? first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and...
content:
Bitcoin’s price could be due a move upwards as the supply of the leading cryptocurrency on exchanges shrinks. 

That’s according to a researcher at data firm CryptoQuant, who wrote in a Monday report that bitcoin on exchanges has dropped to 2.67 million from 2.8 million since February. 

The price of bitcoin was recently $83,485, unmoved over a 24-hour period but up 8% over the past 30 days after having its best quarter in years. Its surge in August and September has led a number of analysts to declare the bear market is over.  

“If buying demand continues to improve while exchange supply remains low, BTC could benefit from a supply-demand imbalance, creating favorable conditions for a longer-term upward trend,” the report by on-chain researcher Rei Researcher read. 

It added: “More importantly, in recent weeks, bitcoin has recovered from its lows while exchange reserves have continued to decline. This is a notable development, suggesting that the supply readily available for trading is decreasing even as the market recovers.”

The report further noted that it was possible investors were taking bitcoin off exchanges to put in cold storage solutions. 

Bitcoin’s price was mostly trading under $65,000 for the first half of 2026. The coin spent most of this year in a bear market following the all-time high of $126,080 it hit in October 2025. 

But that all changed in August. News that the U.S. Treasury would double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations, weakening the dollar but strengthening bitcoin and other non-yield bearing assets. 

Now, the so-called debasement trade — where investors throw money at an asset to hedge against a currency losing its value — is hot again. Bitcoin is benefiting from the trade, analysts say, as it did in 2024 and 2025. 

Bitcoin’s price is still more than 30% below its record. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking
summary: A recent change in the SEC’s rules on quorum could make it easier for the agency to amend its approach to crypto regulation in the absence of a market structure bill.
content:
After US lawmakers failed to pass a comprehensive digital asset market structure bill, financial regulators stepped up efforts to change rules around the oversight and enforcement of crypto companies and offerings. 

However, the two primary regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), are understaffed at the leadership level, leaving the decisions for regulating aspects of the $3 trillion crypto market largely in the hands of just three individuals, two of whom were nominated by US President Donald Trump. 

At the SEC, two commissioners — Chair Paul Atkins and former Acting Chair Mark Uyeda — remain following the departure of Commissioner Hester Peirce earlier this month. The dearth of leadership at the CFTC is even more stark, with Michael Selig serving as the only Senate-confirmed chair and commissioner since December 2025. The agencies are intended to each have five commissioners.

Both agencies have proposed rules that appear to be attempting to take the place of legislation from Congress in regulating cryptocurrencies. 

The SEC proposed rules to provide companies with a safe harbor from tokens being treated as “investment contracts” in August, and the CFTC followed suit in October, with Selig saying the agency would use its “existing statutory authorities“ to address crypto regulation through proposed rules on exchanges. Atkins added on Oct. 2 that “more regulatory proposals [were] on the horizon” for crypto.

Could one SEC commissioner have the final say on crypto rules?

On Sept. 30, the SEC made these regulatory avenues even easier with a lack of commissioners. The agency released a final rule which went into effect on Oct. 2 that it said amended quorum requirements for what it called “promot[ing] flexibility and finality of agency rulemaking.” The rule reduces the number of commissioners required for a quorum to just one person if only two are present in many cases.

“[...] with now just two commissioners around and it being entirely possible that one of them might have to recuse themselves from an issue (or be otherwise MIA), just one is now enough to pass a formal rule that applies to America’s vast multitrillion-dollar securities markets,” wrote Robin Wigglesworth in an Oct. 5 op-ed for the Financial Times.

Related: Crypto regulation at SEC, CFTC to come down to 3 commissioners following key resignation

Uyeda responded in his own Financial Times op-ed on Sunday, claiming that the SEC’s “commitment to its mission remains unchanged” despite having only two commissioners and no announcement from Trump about additional nominations to fill the empty seats. The policymaker said that the rule change “clarifies that the Commission can establish a quorum if all but one commissioner is disqualified from a matter.” 

“Suggesting that the SEC is ‘hastily revamp[ing]’ its quorum rule so that the remaining commissioners can ‘have their way’ makes for a colourful comparison to fictional dystopian regimes but misleads readers about why the Commission revised its quorum rule and why it’s for the better,” said Uyeda.

As of Tuesday, the White House had not announced any nominations for the SEC and CFTC, potentially leaving the rulemaking process in the hands of just one person at each agency for months, if not longer. Congress still has time to vote on the market structure bill at the center of the controversy, the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, but some experts don’t see lawmakers advancing the legislation in a lame duck session between the 2026 midterm elections and when the next session is sworn into office in January.
