  • Evagoras Kountouris previously served as Group CFO at Markets.com and FxPro.
  • The appointment follows Georgios Papassavas becoming CEO and Mohamed Elgayyar taking the role of Head of GCC and Egypt.

Evagoras Kountouris has joined HFM as Chief of Staff, according to a LinkedIn post published today (Tuesday).

Kountouris joins HFM from Libertex Group, where he served as Chief Strategy Officer and Chief Financial Officer for five years and four months.

London's trading industry is coming home!

His appointment follows other senior management changes at HFM. Finance Magnates reported in June that Georgios Papassavas became CEO after serving as Chief Information Officer. In August, HFM named Mohamed Elgayyar as Head of GCC and Egypt.

Kountouris Held CFO Roles at Markets.com, FxPro

Before joining Libertex Group, Kountouris worked at Markets.com as Group CFO, a board member and an executive director for two years and eleven months.

He previously served as Group CFO at FxPro for five years. Earlier in his career, he worked at PwC as an Assistant Manager in Financial Services for five years and two months.

His career spans senior finance and strategy roles at online trading firms, as well as financial services experience at PwC.

HFM Makes Several Appointments Across MENA

HFM has also made several appointments across its MENA operations. In December 2025, the broker promoted Michalis Papacostas to Regional Head for MENA.

It appointed Jean Nahas as Head of Category in the UAE, where he was tasked with overseeing its licensed entity and Dubai office. Ahmad Qutaishat also joined as Senior Business Development Manager after holding sales roles at ATFX MENA, VT Markets and Equiti Group.

title: Trezor Reduces Number of Resellers Following Ledger Drainage Incident
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Trezor Reduces Number of Resellers Following Ledger Drainage Incident 
Hardware manufacturer Trezor has said it is checking which vendors it works with following reports of lost funds from Ledger models. 
This post Trezor Reduces Number of Resellers Following Ledger Drainage Incide...
content:
Hardware manufacturer Trezor has said it has reduced the number of resellers it works with following supply-chain incidents related to its competitor Ledger. 

The Prague, Czech Republic-based company added in a Tuesday post on X that it was in the process of checking which vendors it works with. 

It added that there were no reports of any issues with Trezor devices. “Let us be very clear: there is not a single piece of evidence that Trezor devices have been compromised,” the company wrote. 

“This is a preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution.”

Signing device manufacturer Ledger last week said it had started an investigation after customers in South East Asia reported they’d lost funds after buying from Malaysia-based reseller, CryptoBilis. 

Ledger then said that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. 

More reports of what appear to be tampered devices have since surfaced on social media but Ledger said Tuesday that only devices sold through CryptoBilis have been linked to lost funds. 

It added that it had only confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one affected user’s device. The implant, according to Ledger, was able to read a seedphrase when it appeared on the device. 

Ledger did not reveal how much money had been lost but blockchain investigator Specter said $86 million had been drained from devices. 

“We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost,” Ledger added on X. “Figures circulating online come from third parties and Ledger has not fully verified them.”

Ledger did not respond to Bitcoin Magazine’s questions. 

CryptoBilis has also stopped selling devices, Ledger added, and advised customers who bought from CryptoBilis to not set up their devices and contact the Ledger support team. 

Criminals have been targeting hardware wallets this year. Hackers in July were able to steal close to $120 million in bitcoin from Coldcard users due to a firmware bug in the devices. 

Canadian company Coinkite, which makes the popular products, said that the bug led to faulty seed generation, allowing hackers to guess investor seedphrases. 

In a separate incident, hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor last month reported that close to 81,000 customers had their details leaked after its third-party fulfillment partner had data stolen. 

Scammers earlier this year were able to get hold of customer information via crypto wallet Ledger’s payment processor Global-e to send phishing emails.  

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Strive reports $208M in warrant exercises as Bitcoin holdings jump 11%
summary: Strive is now the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, with 32,773 BTC, as it continues to expand its treasury through equity financing.
content:
Strive, a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company, increased its holdings by more than 11% last week as investors exercised $208 million in warrants, with Bitcoin purchases outpacing share issuance and giving existing shareholders greater exposure to the cryptocurrency.

In a Tuesday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Strive disclosed that it purchased 3,311 Bitcoin (BTC) in the week ending Oct. 9 at an average price of approximately $84,500 per coin. The purchases brought its total holdings to 32,773 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, according to industry data.

At last look on Tuesday, Bitcoin was trading hands at roughly $83,300 apiece, according to Yahoo Finance data. The Strive (ASST) share price was little changed at $27.52.

Strive Chairman and CEO Matt Cole said on X that investors had exercised $208 million in warrants, with approximately 15.3 million remaining ahead of their Tuesday expiration.

Source: Matt Cole

The company also amended its governing documents to set a binding $100 minimum issuance price for its SATA preferred shares, limiting its ability to issue them below that threshold. Those shares were trading at $99.40, at last look.

Strive’s latest purchases increased its Bitcoin holdings per share even as the company issued additional equity. During the reporting period, its Bitcoin reserves grew 11.2%, outpacing a 9.4% increase in its effective common share count.

Related: Treasury yields at 5% threaten extending Bitcoin’s best quarter since 2017

Michael Saylor weighs in on Strive’s Bitcoin strategy

Strive’s latest purchase drew praise from Michael Saylor, whose company, Strategy, pioneered the corporate Bitcoin treasury model.

“Strive is turning demand for digital equity (ASST) and digital credit (SATA) into demand for Bitcoin,” Saylor wrote on X. “Its hypergrowth shows how the capital markets are accelerating Bitcoin adoption.”

Saylor was referring to Strive’s use of common and preferred shares to raise capital for Bitcoin purchases, a strategy similar to Strategy’s own approach through its MSTR common stock and STRC preferred shares.

Strategy added a comparatively modest 250 BTC to its treasury last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC and maintaining its position as the largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.

Related: Saylor teases Strategy Bitcoin buying after ending September with STRC buybacks

title: Crypto exchange MNX takes on OKX, Bitget offering pre-IPO futures for AI giants
summary: MNX is offering a different way to trade the future valuations of private AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek.
content:
Updated Oct 13, 2026, 2:07 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 13, 2026, 11:52 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • MNX, is a new crypto exchange that offers futures contracts that let investors speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot.
  • Unlike competing perpetual futures, MNX’s contracts expire at the end of 2027 and carry no recurring funding fees, but their settlement prices may differ from the prices investors would pay for private shares.
  • The exchange allows traders to use up to three times their available funds, does not currently serve U.S. customers and plans to expand into markets tied to the broader A.I. economy.

A new cryptocurrency exchange will allow investors to speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence (AI) giants like OpenAI and Anthropic when they go public.

MNX, a new crypto exchange developed by former Manifold executives, went live on Tuesday offering futures contracts tied to OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. The platform, built on MegaETH blockchain, raised $6.4 million from investors led by Village Global in June.

Larger crypto exchanges, including OKX and Bitget, already offer contracts that let traders bet on the value of private AI companies without owning their shares.

Unlike Bitget’s perpetual futures which never expire, MNX offers contracts with expiration dates at the end of 2027 and incur no recurring funding fees. OKX also offers contracts with no expiration dates, but uses a different funding mechanism.

The investment is a bet that financial markets have yet to catch up with the enormous amounts of money flowing into artificial intelligence, according to Village Global.

"AI is driving one of the largest investment cycles in history, despite the financial infrastructure around it remaining quite underdeveloped," said Max Killberg of Village Global. He said the firm sees an opportunity to develop financial markets around AI, rather than simply back another prediction market.

Manifold Markets co-founder Stephen Gruggett told CoinDesk that MNX’s approach is better suited to private companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, whose shares trade infrequently and are difficult to price.

"OpenAI, Anthropic secondaries are illiquid and hard to price," he said. "A perp based on an illiquid, stale price is worse than meaningless: it doesn't behave the way investors expect; it's easy to manipulate; and it may have a very high and unpredictable funding rate."

Traders can also use up to three times their available funds, increasing both potential profits and losses.

Prices are determined by trading activity on MNX rather than an external price feed. If a company remains private when its contract expires, the exchange uses publicly available valuations from funding rounds, investment funds or secondary markets. As a last resort, MNX can determine the settlement price itself, subject to a published review princess.

That means traders could end up settling their bets at a price different from what investors might actually pay for shares in a private transaction.

The exchange does not currently serve U.S. customers, although Grugett said it plans to obtain the necessary licenses.

MNX also aims to offer markets around the wider AI economy, including company revenue, employment, housing, the AI supply chain and computing capacity.

AI has become a huge sponge for investment capital, although exposure to the boom is concentrated in a handful of tech companies. The largest U.S. hyperscalers are expected to spend at least $800 billion this year and more than $1 trillion the next, Bitcoin Suisse’s Crypto Wealth Management Report 2026 shows.

title: Strive Buys More Bitcoin, Crosses 30,000 BTC Mark
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strive Buys More Bitcoin, Crosses 30,000 BTC Mark 
The bitcoin treasury company is still the fifth biggest in the space. 
This post Strive Buys More Bitcoin, Crosses 30,000 BTC Mark  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo.
content:
Nasdaq-listed Strive isn’t slowing down with its bitcoin buys.

The company now has more than 30,000 BTC after buying 3,311 coins last week, according to a Tuesday filing. 

Strive now holds 32,773 coins worth $2.7 billion at today’s prices, keeping its position as the  fifth biggest publicly traded bitcoin company, according to Bitcoin Treasuries. 

Strategy, Twenty One, Metaplanet, and MARA all hold more bitcoin than Strive.  

Strive’s stock (ASST) was trading slightly lower on Tuesday. Unlike other treasuries, though, Strive shares are up significantly this year: year-to-date, ASST has risen by close to 60%. 

A number of top bitcoin treasuries have seen their stock plummet this year since the price of bitcoin took a hit. Some top treasuries have had to sell bitcoin or rethink their model altogether. 

Dallas, Texas-based Strive debuted as an official bitcoin treasury last year, following in the footsteps of software company Strategy, the biggest corporate holder of bitcoin. 

Unlike Strategy, though, Strive hasn’t used debt to buy the cryptocurrency. CEO Matt Cole has described the company as debt-free with zero margin requirements and zero encumbered bitcoin.

Like with other digital asset treasuries, the idea is that investors can get amplified returns from Strive’s stock. 

In January 2026, it completed the acquisition of Semler Scientific in an all-stock deal — the first instance of a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company acquiring another such company. 

The company was founded by former Ohio gubernatorial candidate and tech entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bitcoin keeps up pressure on $84K as US stocks skirt Korea tech sell-off
summary: Bitcoin price action preserved overnight gains as US stocks quickly rebounded after opening lower on the back of Korea’s tech-stock rout.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) continued to target $84,000 at Tuesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks attempted to shake off South Korea’s latest tech rout.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin approached $84,000 once more at the start of US trading on Tuesday, still up by around 2%.
  • US equities avoided a copycat sell-off after Korea’s KOSPI index finished the day down 5.4%.
  • Analysis from CryptoQuant warned of increasing US dollar strength challenging BTC price upside as DXY hit its highest level in 18 months.

S&P 500, Nasdaq brush off KOSPI losses

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD returning to near $83,800 at the start of the US trading session, preserving much of its overnight upside.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Equities opened lower on the day after futures fell during Asia trading after Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index shed 7.4% over two days. Semiconductors led the losses amid mounting fears over AI expenditures and competition from China.

Both the S&P 500 index and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index made early gains to briefly turn green on the day, however, both gauges were off less than 0.5% at the time of writing.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

“The most important development has been not just bond yields going up, but the volatility for bonds... and ​that’s starting to work its way out through asset pricing across the board,” Damien Boey, portfolio strategist at Wilson Asset Management in Sydney, Australia, told Reuters.  He said:

“It’s a very uncomfortable situation on many fronts... maybe AI capex just comes off the boil a little bit, and maybe a few players are casualties in that.”

Bitcoin remained caged around exchange order-book liquidity, which continued to act as resistance above $84,000, per data from CoinGlass.

BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass

Related: BTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week

Dollar strength in focus as DXY hits 18-month highs

Bitcoin bulls are facing a double macro headwind this month, CryptoQuant contributor Darkfost said in market commentary on Tuesday.

With bond yields circling their highest levels in nearly a quarter of a century, US dollar strength has increased markedly. The US dollar index (DXY), which compares the dollar to a basket of US trading-partner currencies, has increased by 5.5% since Sept. 9 and hit 102.57 on the day, its highest levels since April 2025.

US dollar index (DXY) one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

While the traditionally inverse correlation between DXY and BTC has declined this year, the post on onchain analytics platform sees crypto markets suffering from a lack of risk appetite.

“Taken together, these factors constrain the liquidity available to markets and erode institutional confidence, leaving them reluctant to take on more risk.” he wrote in the blog post, adding:

“The climate is therefore unfavorable for Bitcoin, which is perceived as a highly risky asset, while tech (NDX) and the S&P 500, more mature markets, continue to surge and absorb what little liquidity remains.”

title: South Korea Blocks 27 Crypto Exchange Websites, Including KuCoin, BitMart
summary:
South Korea’s
Financial Intelligence Unit has ordered access restrictions on 27 websites
operated by unregistered overseas cryptocurrency exchanges, including KuCoin,
MEXC, Phemex, BingX and BitMart.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The move follows
previous action against offshore exchange...
content:
2026-10-13T17:25:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 15:25 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Unregistered crypto exchange operations can carry penalties of up to five years in prison or a $37,000 fine.
  • Google Play restricted 17 unregistered crypto platforms in March 2025, including KuCoin and MEXC.

South Korea’s Financial Intelligence Unit has ordered access restrictions on 27 websites operated by unregistered overseas cryptocurrency exchanges, including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex, BingX and BitMart.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The move follows previous action against offshore exchanges. In August 2022, the FIU sought to block access to 16 platforms, including KuCoin and MEXC, over alleged failures to meet local requirements.

title: UK crypto trader says almost $800,000 lost in knife assault as wrench attacks proliferate
summary: A crypto trader in the U.K. claimed masked intruders stole nearly $800,000 in cryptocurrency at knifepoint, furthering concerns of "wrench attacks" spreading in the country.
content:
Updated Oct 13, 2026, 2:39 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 13, 2026, 11:24 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • A cryptocurrency trader in the U.K. said armed intruders held him at knifepoint and forced him to transfer about $760,000 in digital assets, though police have not confirmed the account.
  • Such robberies, known as “wrench attacks,” use violence or threats to force cryptocurrency holders to surrender their assets, bypassing digital security measures.
  • Chainalysis estimated that criminals stole more than $30 million through violent attacks in the first half of 2026, with home invasions accounting for 37% of recorded cases.

A cryptocurrency trader in the U.K. claimed to have had almost $800,000 of crypto stolen after armed intruders broke into his home and forced him to transfer digital assets to a specific wallet, highlighting a threat to investors that neither self-custody nor encryption can prevent.

The unidentified trader, pseudonymously “realist” on X, said attackers held him at knifepoint, destroyed his phone and forced transfers of approximately $40,000 from a hot wallet and $720,000 from his Ledger wallet.

The trader shared a Solana wallet address on blockchain explorer Solscan to substantiate his account, though there has yet been no corresponding confirmation from the police or other authorities regarding the incident.

“If you live in the U.K. and do crypto get the f**k out,” he posted.

The incident follows recent reports of a similar U.K. robbery last December, where masked attackers beat a cryptocurrency investor with hammers and threatened to kill his pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds in crypto.

Such crimes, commonly called “wrench attacks,” involve physical violence or threats to compel crypto holders to surrender their assets.

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimates criminals stole more than $30 million through violent attacks in the first half of 2026. Home invasions accounted for 37% of recorded incidents, up from 14% a year earlier.

France emerged as a hotspot for wrench attacks, with Chainalysis documenting at least 30 recorded incidents in the first half of this year.

Blockchain security firm Certik identified 52 verified attacks globally during that period, of which 33 were in France.

The figures suggest physical coercion is becoming an increasingly significant concern alongside wholly digital threats such as hacks, phishing and smart-contract exploits.

The implications for investors extend beyond protecting private keys to keeping holdings confidential, limiting public disclosures about one’s trading activity and separating readily available funds from long-term reserves. However, no individual technical safeguards can eliminate the threat of violence.

title: Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus
summary: Anthropic warned that rogue “AI worms” are months away from the ability to self-replicate and autonomously infect user devices such as home appliances and other internet-connected devices.
content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic warned that self-replicating autonomous AI systems may start spreading across user devices without human intervention, akin to computer viruses. 

Rogue “AI worms” may start autonomously targeting everyday devices, including Android TVs, smart appliances, cameras and other internet-connected devices with basic computing power and weak security, according to a Monday report by researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman for Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.

Small AI models may be “months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices,” which would be a challenging threat as it would have “no centralized point to shut off,” the authors said. 

The warning follows renewed concerns over the growing mathematical capabilities of AI models, which may eventually break the cryptographic signatures used in crypto wallets, threatening about one-third of the Bitcoin supply. 

Almost a third of global Bitcoin supply, or 6.26 million BTC, currently sits in addresses vulnerable to being broken by AI models or quantum computers. However, 4.33 million are exposed because of address reuse, meaning that moving that BTC to fresh wallets would end the exposure, wrote Glassnode co-founder Rafael Schultze-Kraft in a Thursday X post. 

A day earlier, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warned that rapid AI advancements could break the elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) securing cryptocurrency wallets sooner than previously expected and urged users to migrate to fresh wallets.

Dragonfly’s managing partner, Haseeb Qureshi, called the warning “cryptographic doomerism” and said that migrating tokens to fresh addresses was not a real solution against the threat.

title: Trade Republic Undercuts Germany’s 1% Pension Cost Cap with Fee-Free Account
summary:
Trade Republic plans to launch a free retirement investment account in Germany in January 2027, using the country’s pension reform to compete on price for savings that could remain on its platform for decades. 
The Berlin-based neobroker said it would charge no custody or regular savings-plan execut...
content:
2026-10-13T15:54:47.880+02:00

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 13:54 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The account will offer government subsidies and tax-deferred investment growth, with selected ETFs also available without fund costs.
  • For Trade Republic, the account provides a route to attract customer assets that could remain on its platform for decades.

Trade Republic plans to launch a free retirement investment account in Germany in January 2027, using the country’s pension reform to compete on price for savings that could remain on its platform for decades.

The Berlin-based neobroker said it would charge no custody or regular savings-plan execution fees. It also plans to remove fund costs from several dozen selected ETFs supplied by BlackRock, DWS and Vanguard.

Eligible customers could receive government support of up to €540 per year, plus up to €300 annually for each child. People who open an account before turning 25 may also qualify for a one-time €200 starter bonus.

The final amount will depend on the customer’s contributions and personal circumstances.

Reform Opens Pension Savings to Market Investing

Germany’s reform creates a new type of subsidised retirement account designed to lower costs and give savers greater investment choice.

The standard version will carry a 1% cost ceiling, while Trade Republic plans to go further by waiving custody and regular savings-plan execution fees. Selected ETFs will also be offered without fund costs “over the long term.”

The new accounts will allow customers to invest subsidised contributions in equity funds and ETFs without the capital guarantee required under the previous system.

This provides greater exposure to potential market returns, but also means the value of retirement savings can fall.

Investment gains will accumulate without current taxation during the saving period, while qualifying contributions may receive government allowances and tax deductions.

Other Brokers Move into Pension Accounts

Trade Republic is one of several European brokers expanding into retirement savings. In Germany, Scalable Capital has announced both a standard pension account and a self-directed version.

Account administration and savings plans will be free, while the fund costs of selected ETFs from BlackRock, DWS, Vanguard and Scalable will be reimbursed and reinvested.

Outside Germany, Trading 212 recently secured FCA approval to offer self-invested personal pensions in the UK. The British and German products operate under different tax and regulatory systems, but both add tax-advantaged retirement savings to platforms built primarily around retail investing.

For Trade Republic, the pension account continues its expansion beyond transactional brokerage into longer-term savings and banking services. The company has also introduced current accounts in markets including Greece.

Germany enacted the reform in May, and the new products are due to become available from 1 January 2027.

The full scope of its fee-free offer will become clearer when the company publishes the eligible ETF list, the duration of the fund-cost waiver and the detailed terms before launch.

title: From Raw Data to Actionable Insights: The Acuity Advantage
summary:

A...
content:

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 12:11 GMT by OneRoyal

Disclaimer

  • OneRoyal’s suite of Acuity AI trading tools helps traders make sense of fast-moving markets, turning news and data into insights that support more informed decisions.

Access to market information has never been easier. However, making sense of that information remains one of the most demanding parts of trading. The sheer volume of corporate announcements and geopolitical developments often leaves traders with more information than they can realistically assess.

A single headline can prompt a price move across several markets. It’s understanding why it matters and whether it changes an existing trading view that takes time. By the time a trader has analysed the news and compared the relevant charts, the market may already have moved again.

As AI makes advanced market analysis more accessible, its practical value lies in helping traders bridge this gap between information and action. For both beginners and experienced traders, the challenge is translating a continuous flow of data into something useful for their strategy.

Through its partnership with Acuity Trading, OneRoyal brings this capability into the trading workflow. Its suite of tools, including SignalX, AssetIQ, Action News, Market Scanner, and Daily Intel, helps traders put market developments into context and identify ideas worth exploring.

Making market information useful

Manual research requires traders to piece together information from different sources. They have to find news feeds explaining the latest developments and a chart showing the price response, all while analysing whether the move reflects a broader trend. The lengthy process can leave traders falling behind.

OneRoyal’s Acuity suite uses machine learning to analyse the latest news across thousands of markets in real time, providing context for price movements alongside actionable trade ideas. This gives traders a more focused starting point for their own assessment.

Action News, for example, helps filter the flow of headlines so traders can concentrate on developments relevant to the markets they follow. Around a major economic release, that focus can help them assess the news alongside the price response.

SignalX and AssetIQ bring further perspective through insights into sentiment, trends, price patterns, and key levels. These inputs can help traders examine whether a potential opportunity supports their existing market view or gives them a reason to reconsider it.

Even though an actionable insight provides a basis for evaluation, traders still need to decide for themselves whether an idea fits their objectives and timeframe.

Analysis that fits the strategy

For analytical tools to become useful on a day to day basis, they need to work within a trader’s existing routine. Constantly switching between research sources can interrupt that process, especially when market conditions are changing quickly.

OneRoyal’s suite is designed to integrate into traders’ strategies, making relevant intelligence easier to incorporate into their analysis. Market Scanner supports this process by summarising data across thousands of assets and highlighting strategy-specific trade ideas. Alongside Daily Intel and the wider suite, it gives traders additional resources for keeping their research current.

For a beginner, this can make the research process more approachable by providing specific developments and signals to investigate. An experienced trader can use the same tools to narrow a watchlist or identify a market that warrants closer attention.

Take the example of a trader monitoring an asset ahead of an economic announcement. Relevant news and key price levels can help them prepare scenarios before the release. As new information arrives, they can assess it against that preparation and decide whether their original reasoning is justified.

Supporting a more proactive approach

The ability to process information quickly gives traders more time to consider its implications. Reacting to a headline without understanding its context often leads to poorly considered decisions.

AI cannot remove market uncertainty or guarantee a successful trade. It can, however, make the analytical work more manageable, helping traders evaluate potential opportunities and adjust their views as conditions change.

By integrating Acuity’s analytical capabilities into its offering, OneRoyal supports this more proactive approach to trading. With less time spent gathering and interpreting raw data, traders have more room to assess opportunities against their strategy and make informed decisions.

title: Exclusive: Crypto Market Maker Wincent Plans US Push After 80% Staff Growth Since 2024
summary:
Wincent, a crypto market maker based in Gibraltar, is preparing to expand into the United States and is studying a move into traditional financial markets. Chief Executive Tom Mazur outlined the plans to FinanceMagnates.com after a rebrand on September 30.
"We have become a much larger and more inst...
content:
2026-10-13T14:00:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 13/10/2026 | 12:00 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • "Market making and trading are what we do," Tom Mazur told FinanceMagnates.com.
  • Shawn Egger, who helped build Citadel Securities’ FX sales business, will lead the expansion into America.

Wincent, a crypto market maker based in Gibraltar, is preparing to expand into the United States and is studying a move into traditional financial markets. Chief Executive Tom Mazur outlined the plans to FinanceMagnates.com after a rebrand on September 30.

"We have become a much larger and more institutional business," Mazur said.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Its over-the-counter (OTC) desk already trades with retail brokers, CFD providers, banks and exchange-traded fund issuers, Mazur said in written answers to questions.

In March, Wincent opened its crypto pricing to CFD platforms through a deal with Wyden, and it now reports more than $5 billion in average daily notional volume across over 15 exchanges and venues.

The firm trades through Wincent Investment Fund PCC Limited, an Experienced Investor Fund regulated by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC). Founders, management and staff provide a large share of the fund's capital, according to Mazur, and the fund is closed to new investments.

Former Citadel Executive to Lead US Push

Shawn Egger has joined Wincent to lead the US expansion, Mazur said, adding that Egger previously held senior roles at Citadel and Crypto.com.

"My mandate is to build and expand Wincent’s presence across the United States, with a focus on institutional relationships, market making, liquidity, tokenization and financial infrastructure," Egger wrote on his LinkedIn last week.

Egger worked in FX sales at Citadel Securities from 2014 and moved to Jefferies as a senior vice president in its forex sales team in 2018. Two years later, crypto prime broker SFOX hired him to run execution services, Hedgeweek reported.

The only regulator Wincent names is the GFSC. Mazur said the firm reviews the rules in each market where it operates or sees room to grow, and has no further licensing announcements to make.

Wintermute took a registered route into the same market. It set up a US headquarters in New York in May 2025 and hired a former Blockchain Association director to run policy.

In August, its subsidiary Wintermute USA LLC registered as a broker-dealer with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which lets it trade US equities and exchange-traded products.

SBI-owned B2C2 named a chief executive for its US unit in New Jersey in September 2024.

Headcount Up 80% Since 2024

Wincent employs 173 people, up from 96 in 2024 and 150 in 2025, Mazur said. The staff work across quantitative research, trading, engineering, institutional business development and support.

"We have become a much larger and more institutional business," Mazur told FinanceMagnates.com.

The firm says it trades more than 300 digital assets, executes over a million trades a day and has more than $750 million in deployed capital. When it joined Wyden's network in March, it cited roughly 500,000 trades alongside the same $5 billion volume figure.

Brothers Matus and Michal Kopf founded Wincent in 2017 as a manual trading operation, Hedgeweek reported.

Both remain on the leadership team as co-founders running investments, while Mazur said he took over as chief executive in July.

"We have no intention of losing the entrepreneurial mindset," he said, pointing to the speed and appetite for calculated risk that built the firm.

New offices will follow only where there is a clear commercial case, according to Mazur. He gave no timeline for the US expansion.

A Trading Firm Inside a Fund

The rebrand release described Wincent as both "a global investment fund" and "a global digital asset trading firm." Mazur called it a high-frequency trading firm first and said the fund is simply how it organizes its capital.

"Market making and trading are what we do," Mazur said.

Crypto market making stays the priority, he said, but Wincent is selectively looking at tokenized assets and traditional markets where institutions want deeper liquidity.

"Any expansion into adjacent markets will build on that foundation rather than come at its expense," Mazur said.

Traffic also runs the other way. Citadel Securities took a $400 million stake in Crypto.com in July, as Crypto.com pushes into tokenized securities and derivatives.

Wincent's own business has leaned crypto-native. In March, Boris Sebosik, chief business development officer, said about 60% of Wincent's OTC flow came from crypto-native institutions.

He expected banks adding retail crypto products to shift that mix. Mazur now lists asset managers, hedge funds, token issuers, miners and fintechs among its counterparties, alongside exchanges.

Serving that range requires access to global banking rails, which Mazur said the firm has worked on for years.

Beyond the US, Wincent lists offices in Zurich, London, Bratislava, Warsaw, Dubai and Hong Kong, among other cities. The rebrand swaps the firm's gold for deep blue and redraws its dragon logo in a more geometric form, with the new identity rolling out already.

title: South Korea blocks 27 crypto exchanges, including Bitmart and Kucoin
summary: The country’s regulators are stepping up their earlier restrictions on mobile apps to websites, targeting unregistered exchanges before investors report losses.
content:
Oct 13, 2026, 7:58 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • South Korea is blocking the websites of 27 unregistered cryptocurrency exchanges, including KuCoin, BitMart and MEXC, after restricting access to their mobile apps last year.
  • Foreign exchanges must register with the Financial Intelligence Unit and meet security and anti-money-laundering requirements to legally serve South Korean customers.
  • Regulators warned that customers of unauthorized platforms may struggle to recover funds and urged investors to verify registration and withdraw their assets.

South Korea is blocking access to 27 unregistered crypto exchanges' websites, including KuCoin, BitMart, and MEXC, extending its crackdown on foreign trading platforms beyond just their mobile apps.

The country’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) announced Tuesday that the Korea Communications Standards Commission approved the restrictions following reviews on Oct. 6 and 7. Websites operated from overseas will be blocked, while those operating domestically face service termination, the FIU noted.

The move closes another route for South Korean investors to access unregistered exchanges after authorities restricted access to their mobile apps on Google and Apple last year. Regulators can now seek website blocks as soon as they detect unregistered activity, without waiting for a court ruling or evidence that customers have lost money.

The FIU did not specify how long the restrictions will last or set a deadline for the exchanges to register. However, any exchange that wants to legally operate in the country and serve South Korean customers must register with the FIU and meet the country’s security and anti-money laundering (AML) requirements.

“We respect applicable laws and regulations across jurisdictions and continuously strengthen our compliance framework in response to evolving regulatory requirements,” a KuCoin spokesperson said.

“User assets remain safe and secure, and we will communicate any further updates through our official channels.”

BitMart, Phemex and MEXC did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment.

South Korea's proposed Digital Asset Basic Law, yet to come into force, would set the groundwork for a legal framework for digital assets, including issuance, trading, custody and supervision. The country’s Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory service announced new rules in April, removing the discretion exchanges had to let users bypass holding periods.

The FIU said it has referred 44 unregistered operators to investigators and will seek further blocks against websites that reopen under different addresses. Only 28 virtual asset service providers are currently registered with the regulator.

The financial watchdog also warned that traders using unauthorized platforms could face difficulties recovering their funds. The FIU said it will work with the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA), an industry association, to help affected customers withdraw their funds where access restrictions create problems. It also urged investors to check whether their exchange is registered and to withdraw assets from unauthorized operators.

South Korean investors have been gradually moving large amounts of crypto overseas for months due to stricter rules, with an estimated $110 billion leaving domestic exchanges in 2025.

title: Federated Hermes joins Wall Street's tokenization push with plans for first onchain fund shares
summary: The $911 billion Pittsburgh-based asset manager is teaming up with Prometheum to bring blockchain-based share classes of its funds to traditional brokerage accounts.
content:
Oct 13, 2026, 7:56 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Investment manager Federated Hermes plans to issue its first tokenized fund share classes in early 2027, building on earlier efforts to bring its investment products onchain.
  • The firm aims to issue tokenized fund shares itself, moving beyond past arrangements where third parties tokenized its existing products, Kevin Barr, director of digital asset products and platform told CoinDesk.
  • Prometheum will provide regulated brokerage, custody and clearing services to help bring the products to financial advisers and their clients.

Federated Hermes (FHI), the Pittsburgh-based investment manager overseeing $911 billion in assets, plans to issue its first tokenized fund shares early next year, joining Wall Street's growing push to bring traditional investments onto blockchain rails.

The asset manager has partnered with plans to make the upcoming products available through traditional brokerages and financial advisers alongside New York-based digital securities infrastructure provider Prometheum, the companies told CoinDesk Tuesday.

The firm has not yet disclosed which funds it plans to tokenize or which blockchains they will use. Money market funds are a likely starting point, Kevin Barr, Federated Hermes' director of digital asset products and platform, told CoinDesk in an interview.

“There's enormous interest in the industry at large around tokenized money market funds, [and] it aligns very well with the ballast of our franchise, which has been our liquidity funds,” Barr said.

The move adds another major asset manager drawn to Wall Street's tokenization effort. Firms including BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, JPMorgan and, more recently, New York Life Insurance Company have embraced blockchain-based versions of traditional funds, betting the technology can modernize how assets are issued, transferred and settled. Using blockchains for investment funds could settle faster, automate recordkeeping and move more easily between financial platforms, proponents say.

Citi has projected that the tokenized securities market could balloon to $5.5 trillion by 2030.

In-house tokenization

Federated Hermes have already experimented with tokenization, and its latest effort goes beyond previous its blockchain initiatives.

The firm has worked with platforms including London-based Archax, Goldman Sachs (GS) and Singapore-based Conduit Digital to create tokenized representations of its existing investment products. Those arrangements involved third parties issuing digital versions of conventional fund holdings.

Federated Hermes now intends to issue tokenized fund share classes itself, Barr said, giving the asset manager a more direct role in bringing its products onchain. Before joining the asset manager in May, Barr spent 15 years at custody banking giant BNY, most recently as head of digital cash and innovation.

The firm's large liquidity-management business makes money market funds a natural starting point, Barr said. Such funds invest in short-term debt and serve as a place for investors to park cash while earning yield.

Tokenized money market funds and U.S. Treasuries have spearheaded Wall Street's tokenization efforts, allowing companies and institutional investors to earn yield on cash reserves while moving assets around the clock. The tokens can also serve as collateral for loans or trades, helping firms put their cash to work without selling their holdings.

"You can have instantaneous movement of those funds," Barr said. "You can have programmability of those funds in a way that is perhaps more difficult or operationally inefficient with traditional infrastructure."

Brokerage accounts access

A key part of the Prometheum partnership is making those products available through familiar investment channels.

Prometheum's SEC-registered broker-dealer subsidiaries will provide custody, clearing and settlement services, while its correspondent clearing platform will allow other broker-dealers to offer Federated Hermes' tokenized products to their customers.

Barr said one of the main barriers to wider adoption has been access, rather than the underlying blockchain technology. Financial advisers and brokerages need ways to offer tokenized funds without rebuilding their systems.

"For us, it becomes a natural extension of how we distribute our products today, and it just makes all the sense of the world from that perspective," Barr said.

For Federated Hermes, the longer-term opportunity extends beyond distributing existing investment products in a new format. Barr said he sees tokenization changing how investors manage cash, move between assets and build portfolios.

"Tokenization represents, in a lot of ways, a fundamental upgrade to financial market infrastructure for this generation," he said.

title: Stacks' STX, a Bitcoin layer-2 token, has surged by 50% in four weeks
summary: Your day-ahead look for Oct. 13, 2026
content:
Oct 13, 2026, 7:26 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

While major cryptocurrencies remain choppy, STX, the native token of the Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, is rallying. The cryptocurrency has surged nearly 10% in 24 hours, 14% over the past week and more than 50% in four weeks, outperforming bitcoin BTC$83,308.26, ether ETH$2,505.48, XRP (XRP) and other cryptocurrencies.

The outperformance likely reflects investor interest in Stacks’ non-custodial bitcoin staking architecture. This framework lets BTC holders stake and earn yield directly on the main Bitcoin blockchain while retaining strict control of their private keys. In contrast, traditional frameworks require users to wrap their assets into synthetic tokens (like wBTC) or move funds over cross-chain bridges to earn additional yield.

Stacks’ framework relies on a mechanism called "bonding," which requires participants to lock up assets to secure the network. The "Bonding Period 3,” due in November, requires participants holding native STX to lock a specific ratio of STX alongside their BTC — equivalent to roughly 5% of the total value of their BTC — to successfully secure protocol stacking capacity.

This creates a positive feedback loop for STX: As more BTC moves into the Stacks ecosystem, a larger portion of STX is systematically locked up and removed from the active market. By tying bitcoin liquidity directly to STX scarcity, the architecture skews demand-supply dynamics heavily in favor of long-term price appreciation.

Period 3 follows Periods 1 and 2, which served as preparatory phases to safely transition signers and bootstrap initial liquidity.

STX is not the only coin to have surged over 24 hours. BDX, REDNER, and PYTH are other major gainers, adding 6% each. It’s a sign of liquidity increasingly pivoting to coins other than the major cryptocurrencies.

Still, the broader context remains tightly bound to macroeconomic indicators. Analysts are getting ready for Wednesday’s U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, which could heavily influence expectations for upcoming Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions. Stay alert!

Table of Contents

  • First Up: Moonflower Coffee Setup
  • The Friction: Fifth House Coffee
  • Bitcoiners Can Lose
  • Have a Story or a Local Merchant to Feature?
  • Appendix: 300 Colorado Bitcoin Merchants

    Exploring the growing network of Colorado Bitcoin merchants was an eye-opening trip that showed me both the immense promise and the friction points of real-world adoption in the Mile High State. Flying into Colorado, I was excited to experience the fall mountains, see my old friends, and dive into the local Bitcoin scene.

    First Up: Moonflower Coffee Setup

    The first stop on my list was Moonflower Coffee. Pulling up, I thought I had mistaken it for an auto-mechanic (FYI there’s a giant oil change sign and two bay garage look). Built inside a beautifully repurposed old auto body shop, Moonflower nails the ambiance: great coffee, a fantastic local vibe, and a spacious lounge area .

    Like many modern registers, their Square terminal had native Bitcoin settings toggled on from the encouragement of local bitcoiners. Instead of selecting the “Pay with Bitcoin” option myself, I asked the barista to enable it on her side. That led to a nice 30-second conversation about Bitcoin before I enjoyed my Black Sesame Mocha Latte.

    Another great option is Butcher Block Cafe, 5002 Washington St, Denver, CO 80216. They had a great breakfast and a classic diner feel, but be sure to go to this location. Apparently it’s family-run and their other location does not accept bitcoin… yet!

    The Friction: Fifth House Coffee

    The contrast between Moonflower Coffee and Fifth House highlighted just how uneven adoption remains.

    Fifth House Coffee has a one screen Square register that doesn’t face the customer, so I couldn’t even select BTC on my own if I tried. When I asked if they accepted Bitcoin, the owner stated firmly that it was his shop and he would not take it. It was on the BTC Map, and has a Square register where the bitcoin acceptance feature likely was updated automatically in the background. I had to walk out without ordering. I still recommend to go stop by and ask about bitcoin.

    Bitcoiners Can Lose

    Reflecting on my time with Colorado Bitcoin Merchants, it forced a critical realization about where real-world adoption is heading. Some people may reject bitcoin on the surface and it’s up to us to dig deeper. We have a window before legacy banking rails step in to capture and monetize this infrastructure. If Bitcoiners want an open source, hard money world, we have the responsibility to create hyperbitcoinization.

title: Justin Sun’s $2.25B Crypto Portfolio Includes $1.09B in SUSDS Across 10 Blockchains
summary:
Key Takeaways: Earlier, Arkham reported that it tracks around $2.25 billion worth of on-chain assets for Justin Sun, spanning 10 different blockchain networks. The bulk of the portfolio (around $1.09
The post Justin Sun’s $2.25B Crypto Portfolio Includes $1.09B in SUSDS Across 10 Blockchains appeare...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Earlier, Arkham reported that it tracks around $2.25 billion worth of on-chain assets for Justin Sun, spanning 10 different blockchain networks.
  • The bulk of the portfolio (around $1.09 billion) is in SUSDS with $607.55 million in STETH and $336.73 million in BTC.
  • In September, Arkham said that its research team had ranked him second to Satoshi Nakamoto, and ranked 211 addresses that were linked to him.

According to blockchain intelligence platform Arkham, Justin Sun, founder of TRON, owns over $2.2 billion in cryptocurrency assets. The data underscore the extent of his positioned estates as well as the share of his wealth maintained in stable coin related and Ethereum associated resources.

  • Arkham Tracks $2.25 Billion Across 10 Chains
  • SUSDS and STETH Dominate Sun’s Portfolio
    • Stablecoin Exposure Stands Out
    • On-Chain Data Offers a Window into Crypto Wealth

Arkham Tracks $2.25 Billion Across 10 Chains

Arkham announced the figures on X, stating that it had labeled approximately $2.25 billion in wallets linked to Sun across 10 blockchain networks. Its dashboard displays a portfolio value of around $2.246 billion and identifies 211 associated addresses.

JUSTIN SUN HOLDS $2.2 BILLION ON-CHAIN

Arkham has labelled $2.25B of Justin Sun’s wallets across 10 chains. He’s the founder of TRON, CEO of BitTorrent and owner of two crypto exchanges.

Our research team ranked him second only to Satoshi Nakamoto in September. https://t.co/EvSkbZ5vLT

— Arkham (@arkham) October 12, 2026

The figures are of assets that Arkham reports holding on Sun, and not a public statement of his total net worth. The market price and transfers transmit the balance of the circulation of wallets as well.

In its black-and-white depiction, Sun is said to be TRON’s founder, BitTorrent’s CEO and the owner of two crypto exchanges. Additionally, the platform states that his research team had ranked him second only to Satoshi Nakamoto in September, but even this may not be an independently released wealth ranking.

Read More: Justin Sun Files $45M Lawsuit Over Frozen WLFI Tokens in Trump-Linked Clash

SUSDS and STETH Dominate Sun’s Portfolio

The dashboard shows a high asset concentration in the limited number of assets. SUSDS makes up the biggest spot, followed by STETH and Bitcoin.

According to Arkham, SUSDS currently holds Sun’s biggest stake of 986.337 million tokens valued at $1.09 billion. His portfolio also includes 238,861 STETH valued at $607.55 million, 4,042 BTC worth $336.73 million, and 1,690 WBTC valued at $140.64 million. Other smaller investments are the 544.719 million WLFI at $31.03 million, the 39.226 million STRX with a value of $17.34 million, and the 6.875 million TRX valued at about $2.28 million.

Read More: FDUSD in the Crosshairs: Justin Sun’s $500M Fraud Accusation and First Digital’s Rebuttal

Stablecoin Exposure Stands Out

This is because SUSDS represents almost half of the monitored portfolio and is the most important position on the dashboard. The token is linked to Sky’s savings stablecoin platform and STETH is a staked Ether asset exposure.

The holdings prove that Sun is not just holding the native token, TRX, of the TRON network. But the balance of wallets says nothing about whether positions are held for investment, how many are used in treasury or are used for collateral purposes.

On-Chain Data Offers a Window into Crypto Wealth

Blockchain explorers allow researchers to monitor public addresses, token balances, and transfers across supported networks. Arkham’s labels aid in the connection of addresses that have been known to the same entity without focusing just on individual wallets.

Nevertheless, there are some restrictions to address attribution. Assets can exist in hides, custodians or organizations with complicated ownership structures and not all wallets are identifiable with an individual.

Arkham’s latest snapshot therefore offers a detailed look at the crypto assets it associates with Sun, while leaving his complete financial position beyond the reach of on-chain balances alone.

Geneva, Switzerland, October 12, 2026 — TRON DAO, the community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet through blockchain technology and decentralized applications (dApps), today highlighted key findings from its State of TRON Q3 2026 ecosystem report. The report examines network activity, stablecoin settlement, liquidity, tokenomics, developer activity, decentralization, and protocol governance during the third quarter of 2026.

TRON surpassed $30 trillion in cumulative transaction volume in Q3 2026, marking another milestone for a network used as infrastructure for stablecoin settlement and digital-asset transfers. At the same time, stablecoin supply and total value locked continued to expand, while the network’s active-address base grew and transaction activity remained broadly steady.

Key Insights

  • In Q3, TRON surpassed $30 trillion in cumulative transaction volume. Stablecoin settlement reached $2.21 trillion in the Q3 reporting period, with average daily volume rising 3.9% from Q2 to $24.05 billion.
  • Canary Capital launched the Canary Staked TRX ETF (TRXS) on September 9, 2026. TRXS gives investors exposure to the spot price of TRX—the native utility and governance token of the TRON blockchain network—alongside passive net staking rewards reflected directly in the fund’s daily net asset value. TRON DAO’s team rang the Cboe Closing Bell in Chicago on September 29 to celebrate its launch.
  • TRON expanded its ecosystem collaborations in Q3 2026, adding institutional custody and staking, new trading venues, and digital dollar products through Anchorage Digital, Bitnomial, Backpack, Ethena, and Ducat. Payment, wallet, cross-chain, and developer integrations also broadened access and strengthened the infrastructure for payment, treasury, and DeFi applications. 
  • Stablecoin supply and Total Value Locked continued to expand. USDT and USDD supply reached $93.88 billion, up 5.5% from Q2, while TVL including staking hit $28.21 billion and TVL excluding staking (DeFi TVL) hit $13.05 billion
  • The active-address base widened while transaction frequency held steady. Average rolling monthly active addresses increased 9.8% to 18 million. 
  • Network fee generation moderated. Fees totaled $701.4 million during Q3, averaging $7.62 million per day, down 4.0% from Q2. The average daily transaction fee fell from $0.668 to $0.643. 

TRON’s ecosystem continued to broaden in Q3, with new integrations spanning institutional services, trading, stablecoins, payments, wallets, and developer infrastructure. Anchorage Digital added TRX staking and TRC-20 custody, while Bitnomial and Backpack expanded access to TRX markets. Ethena brought USDe and sUSDe to TRON, and Ducat connected its Bitcoin-backed financial infrastructure to the network’s stablecoin ecosystem.

The quarter also brought new capabilities for users and developers. MoonPay introduced gasless transactions through Trust Wallet, removing the need to hold TRX for network fees, while Bitcoin.com Wallet added native support for TRX and USDT-TRC20. MetaMask connectivity expanded across B.AI, SUN.io, JustLend DAO, and BitTorrent, while Fireblocks Flow added support for payments from TRON wallets. Eco and STON.fi expanded cross-chain stablecoin connectivity, and KiiChain linked TRON assets with its 24/7 foreign-exchange and payment infrastructure. For developers, Privy expanded wallet, transaction, and policy-management capabilities, while OpenZeppelin brought its smart contract libraries and security tooling to the network. Together, these integrations strengthened the infrastructure available for payments, treasury management, and DeFi applications on TRON.

TRON’s third-quarter developments underscore continued growth in stablecoin settlement, liquidity, network activity, and ecosystem infrastructure, reflecting sustained demand for its financial infrastructure. With these trends strengthening, TRON enters Q4 with an increasingly established role in global stablecoin settlement and digital asset activity.

Read the full report from TRON here.

About TRON DAO

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of October 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 408 million in total user accounts, more than 15 billion in total transactions, and over $28 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”

content:
Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 12, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, concluded its TOKEN2049 Singapore presence with a series of interactive experiences and industry discussions spanning TradFi access, AI-powered trading and the future evolution of global trading platforms.

MEXC’s presence centered on three key areas: the MEXC Stage and a panel featuring MEXC CEO Vugar Usi Zade and Payward Co-CEO Arjun Sethi, hands-on AI experiences including the MEXC AI Trading Challenge powered by MEXC CLI and the AI Bond Test, and The NEXT Newspaper, an interactive experience that brought insights around TradFi, AI and the future of investing into a more engaging community format.

Thousands of participants joined MEXC’s on-site activities during the event, reflecting strong interest in both AI-enabled trading and broader access to traditional financial markets. Across the booth and the MEXC Stage, these themes came together around a broader question: how trading platforms can become more connected, accessible and intelligent as crypto and traditional finance continue to converge.

Exploring AI Through Hands-On Experiences

AI was one of the most visible themes across the MEXC booth.

Through the MEXC AI Trading Challenge, visitors experienced how natural-language instructions, AI agents and MEXC CLI can work together to move trading ideas more directly from analysis to action. The experience demonstrated how users can express what they want to do in everyday language, while AI agents supported by MEXC CLI connect those intentions with MEXC trading capabilities.

Alongside the trading experience, the AI Bond Test offered a more playful way for visitors to explore their relationship with AI, including how they use, trust and interact with AI in everyday decision-making.

Together, the two activities reflected growing interest not only in AI as an information or research tool, but also in how it could become a more natural part of the broader trading experience.

Bringing TradFi Insights Into the Community

Traditional financial markets were another major area of interest at TOKEN2049.

Through The NEXT Newspaper, MEXC transformed research insights around AI, trading and global markets into an interactive experience. Visitors could personalize their own newspaper with their photo and predictions about the future of investing, creating a bridge between research, market trends and community participation.

The activation reflected a broader shift in retail investing as users increasingly look beyond crypto toward stocks, commodities and other traditional financial assets, while expecting to access these opportunities through more seamless digital platforms.

From Crypto-TradFi Convergence to Platform Collaboration

These themes also extended to the MEXC Stage, where MEXC CEO Vugar Usi Zade joined Payward Co-CEO Arjun Sethi.

The panel explored how crypto and traditional finance are moving toward a more connected, always-on financial environment, and how retail demand could help drive the evolution toward platforms that provide access across multiple asset classes.

Arjun highlighted the infrastructure needed to support this evolution, noting that the promise of 24/7 markets ultimately depends on connecting assets and collateral more effectively.

Collaboration was another key theme. Arjun pointed to partnerships as an important part of reaching more global users, specifically referencing MEXC as an example of a platform that could help partners succeed in their respective core markets. Vugar similarly highlighted how platforms can build on different strengths across infrastructure, market access and retail distribution rather than approaching every opportunity purely through competition.

AI also featured in the discussion as part of the longer-term evolution of trading. Vugar noted that AI can help retail users process large amounts of information more efficiently and convert insights into action, while increasingly agentic tools could further change how users interact with financial platforms.

From hands-on AI experiences to TradFi engagement and conversations about the future of market infrastructure, MEXC’s TOKEN2049 presence reflected a broader direction for trading: more connected markets, broader access and increasingly intelligent ways for users to participate.

For more highlights from TOKEN2049 Singapore, watch the event recap video.

About MEXC

Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity.

Singapore, October 12, 2026 – From October 6 to 8, the global crypto industry turned its attention to Singapore for TOKEN2049, a major international industry event. Taking advantage of the gathering, HTX pursued a multifaceted approach encompassing global industry engagement, ecosystem development, and brand awareness. HTX Ventures exhibited at TOKEN2049, where its booth welcomed a steady stream of visitors. HTX DAO hosted “Future Night” and “HTX DAO Reunion,” bringing together industry perspectives and community voices. Meanwhile, a private industry dinner provided an opportunity for invited industry participants, ecosystem contributors, and partners to connect and exchange views. 

From the public stage of a global summit to in-depth exchanges with ecosystem participants and face-to-face conversations with industry peers, HTX’s presence at TOKEN2049 reflected diverse efforts in industry networking, ecosystem development, and partnership building. Beyond providing opportunities for international industry engagement, these events reflected HTX’s ongoing efforts to strengthen industry connections and foster ecosystem collaboration. 

  1. Taking the Global Crypto Stage: Strong Visitor Interest at the HTX Ventures Booth

As a major annual event for the global crypto industry, TOKEN2049 brings together project teams, investment firms, developers, crypto exchanges, and industry builders from around the world. It serves as an important platform for tracking industry trends, forging business connections, and exploring opportunities for global collaboration.

From October 7-8, HTX Ventures, HTX’s global investment arm, exhibited at TOKEN2049 at the Sands Expo and Convention Center in Singapore, with its booth located at Level 5, PB5-47 and PB5-48.

Throughout the event, the exhibition floor remained busy, drawing a steady stream of industry participants. The HTX Ventures booth welcomed numerous visitors, offering an engaging, interactive brand experience through brand displays, on-site community activities , and branded merchandise. These activities encouraged visitors to stop by and connect with the team, bringing the HTX brand into face-to-face interactions with members of the global crypto community.

Meanwhile, Justin Sun, Advisor to HTX, attended related events and delivered a speech before visiting the HTX Ventures booth to engage with the team and other industry participants, further strengthening HTX’s connections with the global crypto industry.

For the crypto industry, the value of an international summit lies not only in raising brand awareness but also in building meaningful connections with industry participants. By combining booth displays, on-site activities, and industry engagement, HTX Ventures brought the brand closer to the global crypto community, creating more opportunities for connections across the investment ecosystem, project discussions, and potential partnerships.

From steady visitor traffic at its booth to a diverse range of on-site activities, HTX Ventures maintained a strong presence at TOKEN2049, providing HTX with another valuable opportunity to strengthen its connections across the global crypto industry.

  1. From Industry Trends to Ecosystem Development: HTX DAO Advances Community Co-Building

While the TOKEN2049 booth served as HTX’s brand showcase to the global crypto industry, the series of events hosted by HTX DAO took these conversations further, exploring broader topics such as industry trends, community building, and ecosystem development.

On the evening of October 6, HTX DAO hosted the “Future Night” event in Singapore. Molly, an HTX DAO ambassador, shared the latest developments in ecosystem mechanisms, community building, and the on-chain ecosystem. Justin Sun, a core supporter of HTX DAO, delivered a video address sharing his perspectives on trends in the crypto industry and the future development of the digital economy.

Sun noted that the crypto industry is deepening its ties with traditional finance, driving the continued digital transformation of global financial infrastructure. AI is changing how wealth is created, while crypto and digital finance are reshaping how wealth is held and transferred.

He further noted that stablecoins could play a greater role in global payments and settlements, while the use of traditional assets such as bonds, funds and gold on-chain will continue to evolve. As AI agents become increasingly involved in economic activity, demand for digital identities, account infrastructure, and the ability to transact autonomously is also likely to grow.

In his view, the long-term value of technology lies in its ability to deliver tangible productivity gains. The free flow of value in the digital world will be a key trend to watch over the next decade.

On ecosystem development, Molly said HTX DAO is exploring potential token utility and ecosystem applications, alongside other initiatives aimed at supporting the development of its ecosystem. For community building, HTX DAO plans to establish regional community hubs in the fourth quarter, enabling members to organize events, exchange ideas, and contribute to the development of the community’s culture. Nearly 200 active volunteers are already contributing to these efforts on their own initiative.

To strengthen its on-chain ecosystem, HTX DAO is engaging university developers from around the world through initiatives such as hackathons. Several projects are currently being explored or developed, including potential applications within the $HTX ecosystem. 

Molly emphasized that ecosystem development requires a long-term commitment. HTX DAO will continue to strengthen its infrastructure, foster an active community, and drive the adoption of ecosystem applications. As an ecosystem participant, HTX continues to gather user feedback and explore improvements to its platform and user experience, with a view to better understanding and responding to evolving user needs. 

From discussions on industry trends to practical initiatives in community development and the on-chain ecosystem, the Future Night event highlighted HTX DAO’s sustained commitment to long-term ecosystem development health  and provided a platform for global community members and industry contributors to connect and collaborate.

III. From Online Communities to In-Person Gatherings: The HTX DAO Reunion Strengthens Ecosystem Connections

Ecosystem growth depends not only on mechanisms and technology, but also on trust among community members and sustained collaboration among participants united by shared goals.

From October 6 to 8, HTX DAO hosted the HTX DAO Reunion, bringing together industry representatives, ecosystem partners, and community members aboard a yacht for face-to-face discussions in an informal setting. 

Unlike traditional conferences built around structured agendas and formal presentations, the event created a more informal setting for participants to exchange views on industry trends, community development, and potential collaborations, fostering a deeper mutual understanding.

For a DAO ecosystem to develop sustainably, community means more than online discussions and on-chain governance. It also depends on meaningful personal connections, ongoing exchanges, and active participation. By creating more diverse opportunities for in-person engagement, HTX DAO is strengthening its ties with community members and partners, opening up new possibilities for community-driven development, ecosystem collaboration, and future partnerships.

From themed discussions to open exchanges, and from online participation to in-person engagement, HTX DAO is exploring diverse approaches to community building and continually strengthening connections among ecosystem participants.

  1. VIP Industry Gathering: Strengthening Face-to-Face Engagement with Ecosystem and Industry Partners

Alongside public engagement with the global industry, HTX also made strengthening relationships with industry peers and partners a priority during Singapore Week.

During the week, HTX hosted a private industry dinner attended by invited industry representatives, ecosystem contributors, and partners. 

Compared with large industry summits, private gatherings provide a more personal setting for direct conversations. These face-to-face interactions allow HTX to listen more closely to partners and exchange views on industry developments, market developments and potential future collaborations.

As the crypto industry evolves, fostering industry relationships requires an understanding of ecosystem developments, effective communication, and the cultivation of long-term partnerships. Face-to-face engagement helps build mutual understanding, laying the groundwork for expanded collaboration across the sector.

From industry discussions at the global summit to in-depth conversations in private settings, HTX is continuously strengthening its relationships with industry partners through engagement at multiple levels.

  1. Driving Long-Term Growth Through Global Engagement: HTX Expands Ecosystem Collaboration

Throughout TOKEN2049 Singapore Week, HTX engaged across multiple fronts, including global industry dialogue, ecosystem development, brand visibility, and industry networking.

HTX Ventures leveraged the international summit to expand its industry network and boost brand engagement through booth activities and in-person interactions. HTX DAO explored industry trends, community building, and the on-chain ecosystem, strengthening connections with community members and developers. It serves over 40 million users across more than 170 countries. Still, people in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and several other blocked regions cannot open or use an account.

In this MEXC review, we will cover its fees, supported coins, futures trading, security features, KYC rules, and withdrawal process. You will also learn whether MEXC is safe in your country, who should use it, and which alternatives may suit you better.

What Is MEXC Global Crypto Exchange?

MEXC is a centralized crypto exchange that lets you buy, sell, hold, and trade digital assets from one account. The platform was launched back in 2018 under the name MXC Exchange, then rebranded to MEXC a couple of years later, and it has grown fast ever since.

You get access to spot markets, leveraged futures, savings products, and even a stock-trading arm called RealStocks, all inside one app or website. MEXC mainly built its name around altcoins. It lists new tokens faster than most big-name exchanges.

Now, below is a quick snapshot to give you a first glance at what MEXC actually offers:

Exchange TypeCentralized crypto exchange
User Reach40+ million users; 170+ markets claimed
Supported Coins3,000+ cryptocurrencies
Spot Fees0% maker; 0.05% taker
Futures Fees0% maker; 0.02% taker
Trading FeaturesSpot, futures, trading bots, copy trading, and P2P
Maximum LeverageUp to 200x in eligible regions
Withdrawal LimitsPrimary KYC: 80 BTC; Advanced KYC: 200 BTC daily
